recipes.title: Maustettu hunajaviini (conditum paradoxum)
recipes.description: Kirjan ensimmäinen ohje: roomalainen ateria alkoi tällä hunajalla, pippurilla, sahramilla ja taatelinkivillä maustetulla viinillä.
instructions: Kuumenna hunaja ja 1 dl viiniä kattilassa miedolla lämmöllä koko ajan vatkaten.
Kun seos kiehahtaa, lisää loraus kylmää viiniä, nosta liedeltä ja kuori vaahto. Toista kahdesti tai kolmesti ja anna seistä yön yli; kuori uudelleen.
Lisää pippuri, mastiksi, laakerinlehdet, sahrami ja viinissä pehmitetyt murskatut taatelinkivet.
Sekoita joukkoon loput viinistä ja siivilöi kirkkaaksi (alkuperäisessä hiilen läpi). Tarjoa ennen ateriaa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The composition of [this] excellent spiced wine [is as follows]. Into a copper bowl put 6 sextarii [1] of honey and 2 sextarii of wine; heat on a slow fire, constantly stirring the mixture with a whip. At the boiling point add a dash of cold wine, retire from stove and skim. Repeat this twice or three times, let it rest till the next day, and skim again. Then add 4 ozs. Of crushed pepper [2], 3 scruples of mastich, a drachm each of [nard or laurel] leaves and saffron, 5 drachms of roasted date stones crushed and previously soaked in wine to soften them. When this is properly done add 18 sextarii of light wine. To clarify it perfectly, add [crushed] charcoal [3] twice or as often as necessary which will draw [the residue] together [and carefully strain or filter through the charcoal].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Sextarii. Tor. partes XV; G.-V. pondo XV; List. partes XV ... pondo lib.... qui continent sextarios sex. One sextarius (a "sixth") equals about 1-1/2 pint English. [2] Pepper. Piperis uncias IV--ordinarily our black or white pepper grains, but in connection with honey, sweets, and so forth, the term "pepper" may just as well stand for our allspice, or even for any spicing in general. [3] Charcoal. Still a favorite filterer for liquors. List. Apicius is correct in starting his book with this formula, as all meals were started with this sort of mixed drink. Tor. deviates from the other texts in that he elaborates on the cooking process.

recipes.title: Matkalaisen hunajajuoma (conditum melizomum)
recipes.originalTitle: Honey refresher for travelers (CONDITUM MELIZOMUM VIATORIUM)
recipes.description: Pippurilla maustettu hunaja, joka sekoitetaan viiniin tienvarren virvokkeeksi – ”antaa kestävyyttä jalankulkijoille”.
instructions: Lämmitä hunaja, mausta pippurilla ja kuori vaahto.
Laita kuppiin hunajaa makusi mukaan ja sekoita joukkoon viiniä, kunnes juoma on sopivan makeaa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The wayfarer's honey refresher (so called because it gives endurance and strength to pedestrians) [2] with which travelers are refreshed by the wayside is made in this manner: flavor honey with ground pepper and skim. In the moment of serving put honey in a cup, as much as is desired to obtain the right degree of sweetness, and mix spiced wine not more than a needed quantity; also add some wine to the spiced honey to facilitate its flow and the mixing.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. Melirhomum; non extat. G.-V. M. perpetuum, i.e., having good keeping qualities. [2] Tor. reads thus whereas others apply "endurance" to the honey itself. The honey could not be preserved (perpetuum) by the addition of pepper. Any addition, as a matter of fact, would hasten its deterioration unless the honey were boiled and sealed tight, which the original takes for granted.

recipes.title: Roomalainen vermutti (absinthium romanum)
recipes.description: Koiruohoviini sahramilla ja mastiksilla – vermutin esi-isä.
instructions: Murskaa koiruoho ja sekoita se mausteiden kanssa viiniin.
Anna maustua viileässä muutama päivä ja siivilöi. Hiilisuodatusta ei tarvita, koska juoma on muutenkin kitkerää.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Roman vermouth [or absinth] is made thus: according to the recipe of camerinum [2] you need wormwood from santo [3] for roman vermouth or, as a substitute, wormwood from the pontus [4] cleaned and crushed, 1 theban ounce [5] of it, 6 scruples of mastich, 3 each of [nard] leaves, costmary [6] and saffron and 18 quarts of any kind of mild wine. [filter cold] charcoal is not required because of the bitterness.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] G.-V. Apsinthium. [2] The mention of a name in a recipe is very infrequent. Camerinum is a town in Umbria. [3] Now Saintonge, Southern France. [4] Black Sea Region. [5] Weight of indefinite volume, from Thebæ, one of the several ancient cities by that name. List. thinks it is an Egyptian ounce, and that the author of the recipe must be an African. [6] Wanting in Tor.; G.-V. costi scripulos senos.

recipes.title: Ruusuviini (rosatum)
recipes.description: Ruusun terälehtiä haudutetaan viinissä kolme viikkoa, ja lopuksi viini makeutetaan hunajalla.
instructions: Poista terälehdistä valkoinen tyviosa. Ompele kolmannes lehdistä liinapussiin ja upota viiniin viikoksi.
Vaihda tilalle tuoreet lehdet ja toista vielä kahdesti viikon välein.
Siivilöi viini ja makeuta hunajalla ennen tarjoilua. Käytä vain parhaita, kuivia terälehtiä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Make rose wine in this manner: rose petals, the lower white part removed, sewed into a linen bag and immersed in wine for seven days. Thereupon add a sack of new petals which allow to draw for another seven days. Again remove the old petals and replace them by fresh ones for another week; then strain the wine through the colander. Before serving, add honey sweetening to taste. Take care that only the best petals free from dew be used for soaking.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Used principally as a laxative medicine. List. These wines compounded of roses and violets move the bowels strongly.

recipes.title: Orvokkiviini (violatium)
recipes.description: Kuten ruusuviini, mutta tuoreista orvokeista ja makeutettuna hunajalla.
instructions: Hauduta orvokkeja liinapussissa viinissä viikko kerrallaan, vaihtaen kukat kolmesti kuten ruusuviinissä.
Siivilöi ja makeuta hunajalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: In a similar way as above like the rose wine violet wine is made of fresh violets, and tempered with honey, as directed.

recipes.title: Ruusuviini ilman ruusuja
recipes.originalTitle: Rose wine without roses (ROSATUM SINE ROSA)
recipes.description: Sitruspuun lehdet antavat tuoreelle viinille ruusumaisen tuoksun – 40 päivää myöhemmin se tarjotaan ruusuviininä.
instructions: Upota lehdet viiniin korissa tai liinapussissa.
Nosta lehdet pois 40 päivän kuluttua. Makeuta viini hunajalla tarjoillessa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Rose wine without roses is made in this fashion: a palm leaf basket full of fresh citrus leaves is immersed in the vat of new wine before fermentation has set in. After forty days retire the leaves, and, as occasion arises, sweeten the wine with honey, and pass it up for rose wine.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] A substitute.

recipes.title: Liburnialainen öljy
recipes.description: Tavallinen oliiviöljy maustetaan hienoksi jauhetuilla yrteillä ja suolalla niin, että ”kaikki luulevat sitä liburnialaiseksi öljyksi”.
ingredients: 1 rkl kuivattua isoalantia tai ruusukvittenin juurta
instructions: Jauha juuri ja laakerinlehdet hienoksi jauheeksi.
Sekoita jauhe ja suola öljyyn ja sekoittele kolme päivää ahkerasti.
Anna laskeutua ja kaada kirkas öljy talteen.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
In order to make an oil similar to the liburnian oil proceed as follows: in spanish oil put [the following mixture of] elecampane, cyprian rush and green laurel leaves that are not too old, all of it crushed and macerated and reduced to a fine powder. Sift this in and add finely ground salt and stir industriously for three days or more. Then allow to settle. Everybody will take this for liburnian oil. [1]

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Like the above a flagrant case of food adulteration.

recipes.title: Sameaa viiniä kirkkaaksi
recipes.originalTitle: To clarify muddy wine (VINUM EX ATRO CANDIDUM FACIES)
recipes.description: Roomalainen viinin kirkastus: papujauho ja munanvalkuaiset sitovat sakan.
instructions: Vatkaa papujauho ja valkuaiset sekaisin kulhossa.
Sekoita viiniin ja hämmennä pitkään. Seuraavana päivänä viini on kirkasta; siivilöi. (Viiniköynnöksen tuhka toimii samoin.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Put bean meal and the whites of three eggs in a mixing bowl. Mix thoroughly with a whip and add to the wine, stirring for a long time. The next day the wine will be clear [1]. Ashes of vines have the same effect.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Ex Lister whose version we prefer. He says, Alias die erit candidum while Tor. adds white salt, saying, sal si adieceris candidum, same as Tac. This is unusual, although the ancients have at times treated wine with sea water.

recipes.title: Pahantuoksuinen kalakastike paremmaksi
recipes.originalTitle: To improve a broth (DE LIQUAMINE EMENDANDO)
recipes.description: Jos garum on saanut pahan hajun: astia savustetaan laakerilla ja hunajalla korjataan makua.
instructions: Savusta tyhjä astia kumollaan laakerinlehdillä ja kaada kastike siihen ennen kuin savu haihtuu.
Jos maku on yhä liian voimakas, lisää hunajaa (ja alkuperäisen mukaan tuoretta nardusta tai rypälemehua).
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
If broth has contracted a bad odor, place a vessel upside down and fumigate it with laurel and cypress and before ventilating [3] it, pour the broth in this vessel. If this does not help matters [4] and if the taste is too pronounced, add honey and fresh spikenard [5] to it; that will improve it. Also new must should be likewise effective [6].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] List. Liquamen, id est, garum. Goll. Fish sauce. [2] Tor. Qui liquamen corruptum corrigatur. [3] Dann. Ventilate it. Goll. Whip the sauce in fresh air. [4] List., G.-V. si salsum fuerit--if this makes it too salty--Tor. si hoc nihil effecerit. [5] Tor. novem spicam immittas; List. Move spica; Goll.-Dann. stir with a whip. [6] A classic example of Apician confusion when one interpreter reads "s" for "f" and "novem" for "move" and another reads something else. Tor. is more correct than the others, but this formula is beyond redemption. Fate has decreed that ill-smelling broths shall be discarded.

recipes.title: Lihan säilytys hunajassa
recipes.originalTitle: To keep meats fresh without salt for any length of time (UT CARNES SINE SALE QUOVIS TEMPORE RECENTES SINT)
recipes.description: Tuore liha peitetään hunajalla ja ripustetaan astiassa – talvella säilyy, kesällä vain muutaman päivän.
instructions: Peitä liha kokonaan hunajalla ja säilytä astiassa viileässä.
Ota käyttöön tarpeen mukaan. Kypsä liha säilyy samalla tavalla. (Nykyään: säilytä jääkaapissa ja käytä muutamassa päivässä.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Cover fresh meat with honey, suspend it in a vessel. Use as needed; in winter it will keep but in summer it will last only a few days. Cooked meat may be treated likewise.

recipes.title: Sinappi-hunajaliemi keitetylle lihalle
recipes.originalTitle: To keep cooked sides of pork or beef or tenderloins (CALLUM PORCINUM VEL BUBULUM ET UNGUELLÆ COCTÆ UT DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Keitetty sian- tai naudanliha säilötään sinapista, etikasta, suolasta ja hunajasta tehtyyn liemeen – ”ihmettelet, kun otat sen käyttöön”.
instructions: Sekoita sinappi, etikka, suola ja hunaja.
Upota liha liemeen niin, että se peittyy kokonaan, ja säilytä kylmässä. Tarjoa viipaleina.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Place them in a pickle of mustard, vinegar, salt and honey, covering meat entirely, and when ready to use you'll be surprised.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. Method still popular today for pickling raw meats. The originals treat of cooked meats (Tor. nucula elixa; G.-V. unguellæ coctæ; Tac. nucella cocta). Dispensing with the honey, we use more spices, whole pepper, cloves, bay leaves, also onions and root vegetables. Sometimes a little sugar and wine is added to this preparation which the French call marinade and the Germans Sauerbraten-Einlage.

recipes.title: Suolaliha mietommaksi
recipes.originalTitle: To make salt meat sweet (UT CARNEM SALSAM DULCEM FACIAS)
recipes.description: Suolattu liha keitetään ensin maidossa ja sitten vedessä.
instructions: Keitä suolalihaa ensin maidossa noin 30 minuuttia.
Kaada maito pois ja keitä liha kypsäksi vedessä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
You can make salt meats sweet by first boiling them in milk and then finishing them in water.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. Method still in practice today. Salt mackerel, finnan haddie, etc., are parboiled in milk prior to being boiled in water or broiled or fried.

recipes.title: Paistettu kala etikkaliemessä
recipes.originalTitle: To keep fried fish (UT PISCES FRICTI DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Heti paistamisen jälkeen kalan päälle kaadetaan kuumaa etikkaa – se säilyy pidempään.
instructions: Paista kalat öljyssä.
Kuumenna etikka ja kaada se heti kuumien kalojen päälle. Säilytä kylmässä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Immediately after they are fried pour hot vinegar over them.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

Dann. Exactly as we today with fried herring and river lamprey.

recipes.title: Osterien säilytys
recipes.originalTitle: To keep oysters (OSTREA UT DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Osterit pinotaan pikellä savustettuun, etikalla huuhdeltuun tynnyriin.
instructions: Huuhtele puhdas astia etikalla (alkuperäisessä tynnyri savustettiin ensin pikellä).
Pinoa osterit astiaan ja säilytä kylmässä. (Nykyään osterit syödään tuoreina parin päivän sisällä.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Fumigate a vinegar barrel with pitch [1], wash it out with vinegar and stack the oysters in it [2]

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. vas ascernum, corrected on margin, ab aceto. List. vas ab aceto, which is correct. G.-V. lavas ab aceto; V. the oysters? unthinkable! Besides it would do no good. [2] Goll. Take oysters out of the shell, place in vinegar barrel, sprinkle with laurel berries, fine salt, close tight. V. Goll's authority for this version is not found in our originals. V. There is no way to keep live oysters fresh except in their natural habitat--salt water. Today we pack them in barrels, feed them with oatmeal, put weights on them--of no avail. The only way English oysters could have arrived fresh in Imperial Rome was in specially constructed bottoms of the galleys.

recipes.title: Asafetidaa riittämään (laser-pinjansiemenet)
recipes.originalTitle: Making a little laser go a long way (UT NUCIA LASERIS TOTO TEMPORE UTARIS)
recipes.description: Kallis silfion- eli laser-mauste säilytettiin pinjansiementen kanssa; siemenet imevät aromin ja maustavat ruoan.
instructions: Laita asafetida ja pinjansiemenet tiiviiseen lasipurkkiin.
Kun ruokaan tarvitaan laser-makua, murskaa muutama siemen ja lisää ruokaan. Laita tilalle uusia siemeniä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Put the laser [2] in a spacious glass vessel; immerse about 20 pine kernels [pignolia nuts]

If you need laser flavor, take some nuts, crush them; they will impart to your dish an admirable flavor. Replace the used nuts with a like number of fresh ones [3]

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] List. and G.-V. uncia--ounce. Making an ounce of laser go a long way. Tor. nucea; Tac. nucia. Lister, fond of hair-splitting, is irreconcilably opposed to Tor., and berates Caspar Barthius for defending Tor. List. Quam futilis sit in multis labor C. Barthii ut menda Torini passim sustineat, vel ex hoc loco intelligere licet: Et enim lege modo uncia pro nucea cum Humelbergio, & ista omnia glossemata vana sunt. V. both readings, uncia or nucia are permissible, and make very little difference. We side with Tor. and Tac. because it takes more than an ounce of laser to carry out this experiment. [2] Laser, laserpitium, cf. dictionary. [3] V. This article illustrates how sparingly the ancients used the strong and pungent laser flavor [by some believed to be asa foetida] because it was very expensive, but principally because the Roman cooks worked economically and knew how to treat spices and flavors judiciously. This article alone should disperse for all time all stories of ancient Rome's extravagance in flavoring and seasoning dishes. It reminds of the methods used by European cooks to get the utmost use out of the expensive vanilla bean: they bury the bean in a can of powdered sugar. They will use the sugar only which has soon acquired a delicate vanilla perfume, and will replace the used sugar by a fresh supply. This is by far a superior method to using the often rank and adulterated "vanilla extract" readily bottled. It is more gastronomical and more economical. Most commercial extracts are synthetic, some injurious. To believe that any of them impart to the dishes the true flavor desired is of course ridiculous. The enormous consumption of such extracts however, is characteristic of our industrialized barbarism which is so utterly indifferent to the fine points in food. Today it is indeed hard for the public to obtain a real vanilla bean. Cf. also notes regarding flavoring to Nos. 276-7, 345 and 385.

recipes.title: Säilyvät hunajakeksit
recipes.originalTitle: To make honey cakes last (UT DULCIA DE MELLE DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Hapatetta sekoitetaan jauhoihin ja hunajaan keksitaikinaan, jotta keksit säilyvät.
instructions: Sekoita jauhot, hunaja, juuri ja suola taikinaksi ja anna levätä muutama tunti.
Kauli taikina ja leikkaa kekseiksi. Paista 200 asteessa noin 12 minuuttia.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
To make honey cakes that will keep take what the greeks call yeast [1] and mix it with the flour and the honey at the time when making the cooky dough.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. and Tac. nechon; G.-V. cnecon; Dann. penion.

recipes.title: Pilaantunut hunaja kelvolliseksi
recipes.originalTitle: Spoiled honey made good (UT MEL MALUM BONUM FACIAS)
recipes.description: Roomalainen kauppiaan neuvo: yksi osa huonoa hunajaa kahteen osaan hyvää.
instructions: Sekoita yksi osa huonoa hunajaa kahteen osaan hyvää. (Nykyään: käymään lähtenyt hunaja kannattaa käyttää ruoanlaittoon tai jättää syömättä.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
How bad honey may be turned into a saleable article is to mix one part of the spoiled honey with two parts of good honey.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

List. indigna fraus! V. We all agree with Lister that this is contemptible business. This casts another light on the ancients' methods of food adulteration.

recipes.title: Hunajan laadun koetus
recipes.originalTitle: To test spoiled honey (MEL CORRUPTUM UT PROBES)
recipes.description: Isoalantin varsi kastetaan hunajaan ja sytytetään: hyvä hunaja palaa kirkkaasti.
instructions: Kasta kuivattu kasvinvarsi (alkuperäisessä isoalantti) hunajaan ja sytytä se varovasti.
Jos hunaja on hyvää, se palaa kirkkaasti.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Immerse elencampane in honey and light it; if good, it will burn brightly.

recipes.title: Viinirypäleiden säilytys
recipes.originalTitle: To keep grapes (UVÆ UT DIU SERVENTUR)
recipes.description: Rypäleet upotetaan keitettyyn sadeveteen tiiviissä astiassa; veden voi myöhemmin juoda hunajajuomana.
instructions: Keitä vesi kolmannekseen ja anna jäähtyä.
Laita rypäleet astiaan, kaada vesi päälle ja sulje tiiviisti. Säilytä viileässä ja pimeässä.
Vaihtoehtoisesti peitä rypäleet ohraleseillä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Take perfect grapes from the vines, place them in a vessel and pour rain water over them that has been boiled down one third of its volume. The vessel must be pitched and sealed with plaster, and must be kept in a cool place to which the sun has no access. Treated in this manner, the grapes will be fresh whenever you need them. You can also serve this water as honey mead to the sick.

Also, if you cover the grapes with barley [bran] you will find them sound and uninjured.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. We keep grapes in cork shavings, bran and saw dust.

recipes.title: Granaattiomenien säilytys
recipes.originalTitle: To keep pomegranates (UT MALA GRANATA DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Granaattiomenat kastetaan kuumaan meriveteen ja ripustetaan kuivumaan.
instructions: Kuumenna suolavesi kiehuvaksi.
Kasta granaattiomenat hetkeksi veteen, nosta heti pois ja ripusta kuivumaan viileään paikkaan.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Steep them into hot [sea] water, take them out immediately and hang them up. [tor.] they will keep.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. conditura malorum Punicorum; Tac. mala granata; G.-V. mala et mala granata.

recipes.title: Kvittenit hunajassa ja rypälesiirapissa
recipes.originalTitle: To keep quinces (UT MALA CYDONIA DIU SERVENTUR)
recipes.description: Kokonaiset kvittenit varsineen säilötään hunajan ja keitetyn rypälemehun seokseen.
instructions: Valitse virheettömät kvittenit, joissa on varsi ja lehdet.
Laita ne astiaan ja kaada päälle hunajan ja rypälesiirapin seos. Ne säilyvät pitkään.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pick out perfect quinces with stems [1] and leaves. Place them in a vessel, pour over honey and defrutum [2] and you'll preserve them for a long time [3].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] V. Excellent idea, for the stems, if removed, would leave a wound in the fruit for the air to penetrate and to start fermentation. Cf. also the next formula. [2] G.-V. defritum, from defervitum; defrutum is new wine, spiced, boiled down to one half of its volume. [3] This precept would not keep the fruit very long unless protected by a closefitting cover and sterilization. Cf. No. 24.

recipes.title: Hedelmät hunajaan säilöttyinä
recipes.originalTitle: To preserve fresh figs, apples, plums, pears and cherries (FICUM RECENTEM, MALA, PRUNA, PIRA, CERASIA UT DIU SERVES)
recipes.description: Viikunat, omenat, luumut, päärynät ja kirsikat säilötään varsineen hunajaan niin, etteivät ne kosketa toisiaan.
ingredients: 500 g tuoreita hedelmiä varsineen (viikunat, luumut, kirsikat, pienet päärynät)
instructions: Valitse virheettömät hedelmät varsineen.
Asettele ne purkkiin niin, etteivät ne kosketa toisiaan, ja peitä hunajalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Select them all very carefully with the stems on [1] and place them in honey so they do not touch each other.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] See the preceding formula.

recipes.title: Sitruunoiden säilytys
recipes.originalTitle: To keep citron (CITRIA UT DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Sitruunat laitetaan lasiastiaan, joka suljetaan kipsillä ja ripustetaan.
instructions: Laita sitruunat lasipurkkiin ja sulje tiiviisti.
Säilytä viileässä riippumassa tai hyllyllä. (Alkuperäisessä kansi tiivistettiin kipsillä.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Place them in a glass [2] vessel which is sealed with plaster and suspended.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. conditura malorum Medicorum quæ et citria dicuntur. V. Not quite identified. Fruit coming from Asia Minor, Media or Persia, one of the many varieties of citrus fruit. Probably citron because of their size. Goll. Lemon-apples; Dann. lemons (oranges). List. Scilicet mala, quæ Dioscorides Persica quoque & Medica, & citromala, Plinius item Assyria appellari dicit. [2] G.-V. vas vitreum; Tac. and Tor. vas citrum; V. a glass vessel could not be successfully sealed with plaster paris, and the experiment would fail; cf. note 3 to No. 21.

recipes.title: Mulperinmarjat omassa mehussaan
recipes.originalTitle: To keep mulberries (MORA UT DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Marjat säilötään omaan mehuunsa, joka on sekoitettu puoleen keitettyyn uuteen viiniin.
instructions: Murskaa osa marjoista mehuksi ja sekoita keitettyyn rypälemehuun.
Laita kokonaiset marjat lasipurkkiin, kaada liemi päälle ja seuraa säilymistä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Mulberries, in order to keep them, must be laid into their own juice mixed with new wine [boiled down to one half] in a glass vessel and must be watched all the time [so that they do not spoil].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. This and the foregoing formulæ illustrate the ancients' attempts at preserving foods, and they betray their ignorance of "processing" by heating them in hermetically sealed vessels, the principle of which was not discovered until 1810 by Appert which started the now gigantic industry of canning.

recipes.title: Kasvisten ja yrttien säilytys
recipes.description: Nuoret, ei liian kypsät keittovihannekset säilötään pikellä tiivistettyyn astiaan.
instructions: Valitse nuoria, ei ylikypsiä vihanneksia.
Pakkaa ne tiiviiseen astiaan ja säilytä viileässä. (Nykyään: pakasta tai säilö suolaveteen.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[h]olera ut diu serventur

Place selected pot herbs, not too mature, in a pitched vessel.

recipes.title: Hapro säilöttynä hunajaan ja etikkaan
recipes.originalTitle: To preserve sorrel or sour dock (LAPÆ UT DIU SERVENTUR)
recipes.description: Hapro tai hierakka säilötään myrttimarjojen, hunajan ja etikan kanssa – tai sinappi-hunajaliemeen.
instructions: Puhdista lehdet ja kerrosta ne purkkiin marjojen kanssa.
Sekoita hunaja ja etikka ja kaada päälle niin, että lehdet peittyvät.
Toinen tapa: sekoita sinappia, hunajaa, etikkaa ja suolaa ja peitä lehdet sillä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Trim and clean [the vegetable] place them together sprinkle myrtle berries between, cover with honey and vinegar.

Another way: prepare mustard honey and vinegar also salt and cover them with the same.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] The kind of vegetable to be treated here has not been sufficiently identified. List. and G.-V. rapæ--turnips--from rapus, seldom rapa,--a rape, turnip, navew. Tac. and Tor. Lapæ (lapathum), kind of sorrel, monk's rhubarb, dock. Tor. explaining at length: conditura Rumicis quod lapathon Græci, Latini Lapam quoque dicunt. V. Tor. is correct, or nearly so. Turnips, in the first place, are not in need of any special method of preservation. They keep very well in a cool, well-ventilated place; in fact they would hardly keep very long if treated in the above manner. These directions are better applied to vegetables like dock or monk's rhubarb. Lister, taking Humelbergii word for it, accepts "turnips" as the only truth; but he has little occasion to assail Torinus as he does: Torinus lapam legit, & nullibi temeritatem suam atque inscientiam magis ostendit. Now, if Torinus, according to Lister, "nowhere displays more nerve and ignorance" we can well afford to trust Torinus in cases such as this.

recipes.title: Tryffeleiden säilytys
recipes.originalTitle: To keep truffles (TUBERA UT DIU SERVENTUR)
recipes.description: Tryffelit, joita ei saa kastella, kerrostetaan kuivaan sahanpuruun suljetussa astiassa viileässä.
instructions: Älä pese tryffeleitä.
Kerrosta ne astiaan kuivan sahanpurun (tai riisin) väliin, sulje tiiviisti ja säilytä viileässä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The truffles which must not be touched by water are placed alternately in dry sawdust; seal the vessel with plaster and deposit it in a cool place.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

Dann. Clean [peel] the truffles ... in another vessel place the peelings, seal the vessels.... V. this would be the ruin of the truffles, unless they were "processed" in the modern way. Our originals have nothing that would warrant this interpretation.

recipes.title: Persikat etikassa ja kynteliassa
recipes.originalTitle: To keep hard-skinned peaches (DURACINA PERSICA UT DIU DURENT)
recipes.description: Kovat persikat suolavedessä yön yli, sitten etikkaan suolan ja kyntelin kanssa.
instructions: Laita persikat suolaveteen yön yli.
Huuhtele, asettele purkkiin, ripottele päälle suolaa ja kynteliä ja peitä etikalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Select the best and put them in brine. The next day remove them and rinsing them carefully set them in place in a vessel, sprinkle with salt and satury and immerse in vinegar.

recipes.title: Vihreiden oliivien säilytys
recipes.originalTitle: To keep green olives (OLIVAS VIRIDES SERVARE)
recipes.description: Tuoreet oliivit suolaveteen, jotta niistä voi puristaa vihreää öljyä milloin vain.
instructions: Liuota suola veteen.
Upota oliivit liemeen ja säilytä viileässä. Niitä voi käyttää kuin juuri poimittuja.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
To keep olives, fresh from the tree, in a manner enabling you to make oil from them any time you desire just place them [in brine]. [1] having been kept thus for some time the olives may be used as if they had just come off the tree fresh if you desire to make green oil of them.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] The original does not state the liquid in which the olives are to be placed. Hum. in illud, legendum puto, in muriam. Hum. is correct. Olives are preserved in brine to this day. Schuch's version of this formula (his No. 27) follows our No. 28, together with his own No. 28, To Keep Damascene Plums [etc.] which is wanting in List., G.-V., and all the earlier editions because it is from the codex Salmasianus and will be found among the Excerpts of Vinidarius at the end of the Apician recipes. [CUMINATUM. Hum., List. and G.-V.--Tac. and Tor. at the end of Book I.]

recipes.title: Laser-kastike (laseratum)
recipes.description: Asafetida eli roomalaisen silfionin korvike liuotetaan haaleaan kalakastikkeeseen yrttien, hunajan ja etikan kanssa.
instructions: Jauha pippuri, persilja ja minttu huhmareessa.
Lisää asafetida, hunaja, etikka ja kalakastike ja sekoita. Käytä mausteena lihalle ja kasviksille.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[tor.] laser is prepared in this manner: laser (which is also called laserpitium by the romans, while the greeks call it silphion) from cyrene [1] or from parthia [2] is dissolved in lukewarm moderately acid broth; or pepper, parsley, dry mint, laser root, honey, vinegar and broth [are ground, compounded and dissolved together].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Cyrene, a province in Africa, reputed for its fine flavored laser. [2] Parthia, Asiatic country, still supplying asa f{oe}tida. The African root furnishing laser was exterminated by the demand for it. Cf. Laser in Index.

recipes.title: Toinen laser-kastike
recipes.description: Pippuria, kuminaa, aniksia, persiljaa ja minttua silfionin lehtien kanssa, hunajaa, etikkaa ja garumia.
instructions: Jauha mausteet ja yrtit huhmareessa.
Sekoita joukkoon hunaja, etikka ja kalakastike.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[another laser flavor which takes] pepper, caraway, anise, parsley, dry mint, the leaves [1] of silphium, malobathrum [2] indian spikenard, a little costmary, honey, vinegar and broth.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. Silphij folium; List. Sylphium, folium; G.-V. Silfi, folium, the latter two interpretations meaning silphium (laser) and leaves (either nard or bay leaves) while both Tor. and Tac. (silfii folium) mean the leaves of silphium plant. [2] Malobathrum, malobatrum, malabathrum--leaves of an Indian tree, wild cinnamon.

recipes.title: Viinikastike tryffeleille
recipes.originalTitle: Wine sauce for truffles ({OE}NOGARUM IN TUBERA)
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, korianteria ja ruutaa garumin, hunajan ja öljyn kanssa – tai timjamia ja kynteliä.
instructions: Jauha mausteet huhmareessa.
Sekoita joukkoon kalakastike, hunaja, öljy ja viini ja lämmitä.
Kaada keitettyjen tai paistettujen tryffelien tai herkkusienten päälle. (Toinen tapa: timjamia, kynteliä, pippuria, lipstikkaa, hunajaa, garumia ja öljyä.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pepper, lovage, coriander, rue, broth, honey and a little oil.

Another way: thyme, satury, pepper, lovage, honey, broth and oil.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Also Elæogarum. V. Directions wanting whether the above ingredients are to be added to the already prepared garum, which see in dictionary. Gollmer gives the following direction for garum: Boil a sextarium of anchovies and 3 sextarii of good wine until it is thick purée. Strain this through a hair sieve and keep it in glass flask for future use. This formula, according to Goll. should have followed our No. 9; but we find no authority for it in the original. Oenogarum proper would be a garum prepared with wine, but in this instance it is the broth in which the truffles were cooked that is to be flavored with the above ingredients. There is no need and no mention of garum proper. Thus prepared it might turn out to be a sensible sauce for truffles in the hands of a good practitioner. Note the etymology of the word "garum," now serving as a generic name for "sauce" which originally stood for a compound of the fish garus. Cf. Garum in index.

recipes.title: Juustokumina-inkivääritahna (oxyporum)
recipes.description: ”Helppo kulku” – ruoansulatusta edistävä maustetahna kuminasta, inkivääristä, taateleista, pippurista ja hunajasta.
instructions: Liota kumina etikassa, keitä etikka pois ja jauha kumina.
Survo joukkoon inkivääri, taatelit ja pippuri ja sekoita hunajaan. (Alkuperäisessä myös salpietaria.)
Käytä mausteena tarpeen mukaan.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[tor. Oxyporum (which signifies "easy passage") so named because of its effect, takes] 2 ozs. Of cumin, 1 oz. Of ginger [list. 1 oz. Of green rue] 6 scruples of saltpeter, a dozen scruples of plump dates, 1 oz. Of pepper and 11 [list. 9] ozs. Of honey. The cumin may be either æthiopian, syrian or lybian, must be first soaked in vinegar, boiled down dry and pounded. Afterwards add your honey. This compound, as needed, is used as oxyporum.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

Cf. No. 111, A Harmless Salad. Bran. op. cit., p. 25-6, of Greek origin.

recipes.title: Juusto-pähkinäkastike (hypotrima)
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, minttua, pinjansiemeniä ja rusinoita makean juuston, hunajan, viinin ja garumin kanssa.
instructions: Jauha mausteet, pinjansiemenet ja rusinat huhmareessa tai tehosekoittimessa.
Sekoita joukkoon juusto ja loput aineet sileäksi kastikkeeksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[tor. Hypotrima, meaning in latin a perfect mess of potage, requires this]: pepper, lovage, dry mint, pignolia nuts, raisins, date wine, sweet cheese, honey, vinegar, broth, wine, oil, must or reduced must [2]

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] List. and G.-V. Hypotrimma. V. This formula, lacking detailed instructions, is of course perfectly obscure, and it would be useless to debate over it. [2] Tor. and Tac. cariotam; Sch. cariotum; List. and G.-V. car{oe}num. This (carenum) is new wine boiled down one half of its volume. Cariotum is a palm wine or date wine.

recipes.title: Hapan kalakastike (oxygarum)
recipes.originalTitle: Oxygarum, an aid to digestion (OXYGARUM DIGESTIBILE)
recipes.description: Ruoansulatusta edistävä mausteseos pippurista, kardemummasta, kuminasta ja mintusta, sidottu hunajalla; käyttöön garumin ja etikan kanssa.
instructions: Jauha mausteet yksi kerrallaan ja sekoita ne hunajaan tahnaksi.
Sekoita käyttöön otettaessa kalakastikkeeseen ja etikkaan maun mukaan.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[tor. Oxygarum (which is similar to garum or rather an acid sauce) is digestible and is composed of]: 1/2 oz. Of pepper, 3 scruples of gallic silphium, 6 scruples of cardamom, 6 of cumin, 1 scruple of leaves, 6 scruples of dry mint. These [ingredients] are broken singly and crushed and [made into a paste] bound by honey. When this work is done [or whenever you desire] add broth and vinegar [to taste].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

Cf. Note to No. 33.

recipes.title: Toinen hapan kalakastike
recipes.description: Pippuria, persiljaa, kuminaa ja lipstikkaa hunajaan; käytettäessä garumia ja etikkaa.
instructions: Jauha mausteet ja sekoita hunajaan.
Lisää käytettäessä kalakastiketta ja etikkaa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
1 oz. Each of pepper, parsley, carraway, lovage, mix with honey. When done add broth and vinegar.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Wanting in Torinus.

recipes.title: Yrttitahna huhmareesta (mortaria)
recipes.description: Tuoretta minttua, ruutaa, korianteria ja fenkolia survotaan hienoksi; joukkoon lipstikkaa, pippuria, hunajaa, garumia ja etikkaa.
instructions: Survo tuoreet yrtit hienoksi huhmareessa.
Lisää lipstikka, pippuri, hunaja, kalakastike ja etikka ja sekoita.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Mortaria are preparations made in the mortar. Place in the mortar [tor.] mint, rue, coriander and fennel, all fresh and green and crush them fine. Lovage, pepper, honey and broth [2] and vinegar [3] to be added when the work is done.

[XV]

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

Ex Tor. first sentence wanting in other texts. [1] List. and G.-V. moretaria, from moretum. [2] Dann. calls this "Kalte Schale" which as a rule is a drink or a cold refreshing soup, popular on the Continent in hot weather. Not a bad interpretation if instead of the broth the original called for wine or fruit juices. V. Mortaria are ingredients crushed in the mortar, ready to be used in several combinations, similar to the ground fine herbs, remoulade, in French cuisine that may be used for various purposes, principally for cold green sauces. [3] Wanting in Tor.

recipes.title: Kuminakastike ostereille ja simpukoille
recipes.originalTitle: Cumin sauce for shellfish (CUMINATUM IN OSTREA ET CONCHYLIA)
recipes.description: Runsaasti kuminaa, pippuria, lipstikkaa, persiljaa ja minttua hunajan, etikan ja garumin kanssa.
instructions: Jauha mausteet ja yrtit huhmareessa.
Sekoita joukkoon hunaja, etikka ja kalakastike. Tarjoa ostereiden tai simpukoiden kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: [tor. Cumin sauce (so called because cumin is its chief ingredient) for oysters and clams is made of] pepper, lovage, parsley, dry mint, malabar leaves, quite some cumin, honey, vinegar, and broth.

recipes.title: Toinen kuminakastike
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, persiljaa, minttua ja runsaasti kuminaa hunajan, etikan ja garumin kanssa.
instructions: Jauha mausteet ja yrtit.
Sekoita joukkoon hunaja, etikka ja kalakastike.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pepper, lovage, parsley, dry mint, plenty of cumin, honey, vinegar and broth.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] wanting in List. The cumin sauce formulæ are under chap. XV in G.-V., following our No. 30.

recipes.title: Äyriäistahna lipstikalla ja kuminalla (isicia)
recipes.description: Hienonnetuista meren antimista – hummerista, kalmarista, kampasimpukoista tai ostereista – tehty taikina, maustettuna lipstikalla, pippurilla, kuminalla ja asafetidalla.
instructions: Hienonna äyriäiset tahnaksi.
Mausta lipstikalla, pippurilla, kuminalla ja asafetidalla ja sido munalla.
Muotoile pieniksi pihveiksi ja paista öljyssä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
There are many kinds of minced dishes [1] seafood minces [2] are made of sea-onion, or sea crab-fish, lobster, cuttle-fish, ink fish, spiny lobster, scallops and oysters [3]. The forcemeat is seasoned with lovage [4], pepper, cumin and laser root.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. Sentence wanting in other texts. V. Forcemeats, minced meats, sausage. Tor. Hysitia, from Isicia. This term is derived from insicium, from salsicium, from salsum insicium, cut salt meat; old French salcisse, saulcisse, modern French saucisse, meaning sausage. This is a confirmation of the meaning of the word salsum--meaning primarily salt meat, bacon in particular. It has survived in modern French terminology in salés more specially petits salés--small rashers of bacon. Salsum has caused much confusion in some later formulæ. Cf. notes to Nos. 148, 150, 152. [2] V. fish forcemeats, fish balls, fish cakes and similar preparations. [3] Scallops and oysters wanting in List. and G.-V. [4] Wanting in List.

recipes.title: Kalmaripyörykät
recipes.description: Kalmarin liha survotaan tahnaksi, muotoillaan pyöryköiksi ja keitetään kalakastikkeella maustetussa liemessä.
instructions: Hienonna kalmari ja survo tai jauha tahnaksi. Mausta pippurilla.
Muotoile pieniksi pyöryköiksi.
Keitä pyörykät kalakastikkeella maustetussa vedessä kypsiksi ja asettele kauniisti vadille.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The meat is separated from bones, skin [and refuse] chopped fine and pounded in the mortar. Shape the forcemeat into neat croquettes [2] and cook them in liquamen [3].

They are displayed nicely on a large dish.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. This formula plainly calls for fish balls braised or stewed in broth. Ordinarily we would boil the fish first and then separate the meat from the bones, shred or chop it fine, bind with cream sauce, flour and eggs; some add potatoes as a binder, and fry. [1] G.-V. lolligine; Tor. loligine, which is correctly spelled. [2] Tac. and Tor. in pulmento tundes. G.-V. fulmento which is wrong. Pulmentum, abbreviated for pulpamentum, from pulpa. It means a fleshy piece of fish or meat, a tid-bit. [3] The original says in liquamine fricatur--fry in l., which is impossible in the sense of the word, frying. Either "frying" here stands for cooking, stewing, braising, poaching, or else the so mysterious liquamen must here mean deep fat. Most likely these fish forcemeat balls were fried in olive oil. Cf. {Rx} No. 46.

recipes.title: Hummeri- tai rapupyörykät
recipes.originalTitle: Lobster or crabmeat croquettes (ISICIA DE SCILLIS VEL DE CAMMARIS AMPLIS)
recipes.description: Äyriäisen liha survotaan pippurin ja parhaan garumin kanssa, muotoillaan pikku kakuiksi ja paistetaan.
instructions: Survo äyriäisen liha pippurin ja kalakastikkeen kanssa.
Sido munalla, muotoile pieniksi kakuiksi ja paista öljyssä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The shells of the lobsters or crabs [which are cooked] are broken, the meat extracted from the head and pounded in the mortar with pepper and the best kind of broth. This pulp [is shaped into neat little cakes which are fried] and served up nicely [2].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Scilla or squilla, squill, sea-onion, also a crab, cammarus amplus, large lobster, langouste, spiny lobster. [2] The original omits the mode of cooking the fish. A case where it is taken for granted that the shellfish is boiled in water alive. The broth (liquamen) is a thick fish sauce in this case, serving as a binder for the meat, conforming to present methods. Dann. Fill this into sausage casing. There is no authority for this.

recipes.title: Porsaanmaksanyytit verkkorasvassa (omentata)
recipes.description: Paistettu porsaanmaksa survotaan pippurin ja ruudan kanssa, kääritään verkkorasvaan ja laakerinlehtiin ja savustetaan.
instructions: Paista maksaa kevyesti ja poista kalvot.
Survo pippuri ja ruuta kalakastikkeen kanssa, lisää maksa ja survo tahnaksi.
Muotoile pieniksi makkaroiksi, kääri verkkorasvaan ja laakerinlehtiin. (Alkuperäisessä ne savustettiin.)
Paista ennen tarjoilua ja tarjoa kastikkeen kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Omentata are made in this manner: [lightly] fry pork liver, remove skin and sinews first [2]. Crush pepper and rue in a mortar with [a little] broth, then add the liver, pound and mix. This pulp shape into small sausage, wrap each in caul and laurel leaves and hang them up to be smoked. Whenever you want and when ready to enjoy them take them out of the smoke, fry them again, and add gravy [3].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] From omentum--caul, the membrane enclosing the bowels. Hence "omen." Minced meats wrapped in caul and fried are kromeskis in kitchen terminology. [2] First--an after thought so characteristic in culinary literature, proof enough that this formula originated in a kitchen. The ante tamen of the original belongs to this sentence, not to the next, as the editors have it. [3] Wanting in G.-V. The original continues without interruption to the next, an entirely new formula.

recipes.title: Aivovanukas oreganokastikkeessa
recipes.description: Keitetyt aivot sekoitetaan munien ja mausteiden kanssa vanukkaaksi, paloitellaan ja lämmitetään pippuri-oreganokastikkeessa.
instructions: Survo pippuri, lipstikka ja oregano kalakastikkeen kanssa, lisää aivot ja sekoita kokkareettomaksi. Sekoita joukkoon munat.
Levitä voideltuun vuokaan ja kypsennä 175 asteessa noin 25 minuuttia. Anna jäähtyä, kumoa ja leikkaa paloiksi.
Kastike: kiehauta mausteet liemessä, suurusta ja siivilöi. Lämmitä palat kastikkeessa ja tarjoa pippuria pinnalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[isicia de cerebellis] [1]

Put in the mortar pepper, lovage and origany, moisten with broth and rub; add cooked brains and mix diligently so that there be no lumps. Incorporate five eggs and continue mixing well to have a good forcemeat which you may thin with broth. Spread this out in a metal pan, cook, and when cooked [cold] unmould it onto a clean table. Cut into handy size. [now prepare a sauce] put in the mortar pepper, lovage and origany, crush, mix with broth put into a sauce pan, boil, thicken and strain. Heat the pieces of brain pudding in this sauce thoroughly, dish them up, sprinkled with pepper, in a mushroom dish [2].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] The Original has no title for this dish. [2] List. and G.-V. here start the next formula, but Tor. continues without interruption. Cf. Note 2 to No. 46.

recipes.title: Kampasimpukkapyörykät
recipes.originalTitle: A dish of scallops (ISICIA EX SPONDYLIS)
recipes.description: Kypsät kampasimpukat hienonnetaan speltin ja munien kanssa, kääritään verkkorasvaan ja paistetaan; alle runsas kalakastike.
instructions: Kypsennä simpukat kevyesti ja hienonna ne.
Sekoita spelttiin ja muniin, mausta pippurilla ja muotoile pyöryköiksi.
Kääri verkkorasvaan ja paista öljyssä. Tarjoa kalakastikkeen päällä alkuruokana.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[lightly] cook scallops [or the firm part of oysters] remove the hard and objectionable parts, mince the meat very fine, mix this with cooked spelt and eggs, season with pepper, [shape into croquettes and wrap] in caul, fry, underlay a rich fish sauce and serve as a delicious entrée [2].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Sch. sfondilis; G.-V. sphondylis; List. spongiolis. According to Lister, this is a dish of mushrooms, but he is wrong. He directs to remove sinews when mushrooms haven't any, but shellfish have. Torinus is correct. Gollmer makes the same mistake, believing spondyli to be identical with spongioli. He and Danneil take elixata for "choice" when this plainly means "cooked." If one were not sure of either word, the nature of the subject would leave no room for any doubt. Cf. note 1 to Nos. 115-121. [2] We may find a reason for the combination of these last three distinctly different formulæ into one article in the following explanation. It is possible that these dishes were served together as one course, even on one platter, thus constituting a single dish, as it were. Such a dish would strongly resemble platters of "fritures" and "fritto misto" (mixed fried foods) esteemed in France and Italy. We, too, have "Shore Dinners" and other "Combination Platters" with lobster, crabs, scallops, shrimps, mushrooms, tomatoes--each article prepared separately, but when served together will form an integral part of ONE dish. The above formulæ, though somewhat incomplete, are good and gastronomically correct. A combination of these isicia such as we here suggest would be entirely feasible and would in fact make a dish of great refinement, taxing the magiric artist's skill to the utmost. We would class them among the entremets chauds which are often used on a buffet table or as hot hors d'{oe}uvres.

recipes.title: Porsasnyytit vehnällä ja pähkinöillä
recipes.originalTitle: Another kind of kromeskis (ALITER ISICIA OMENTATA)
recipes.description: Hienonnettu porsaanliha sekoitetaan vehnän ja viinin kanssa, maustetaan pippurilla, myrttimarjoilla ja pähkinöillä ja kääritään verkkorasvaan.
instructions: Sekoita jauheliha, vehnä, viini, pippuri ja kalakastike.
Lisää murskatut marjat ja pähkinät ja muotoile pieniksi rulliksi.
Kääri verkkorasvaan, paista ja tarjoa viinikastikkeen kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Finely cut pulp [of pork] is ground with the hearts [2] of winter wheat and diluted with wine. Flavor lightly with pepper and broth and if you like add a moderate quantity of [myrtle] berries also crushed, and after you have added crushed nuts and pepper [3] shape the forcemeat into small rolls, wrap these in caul, fry, and serve with wine gravy.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Wanting in Lister. [2] Fine wheat flour, cream of wheat. [3] Either pepper corns or allspice. The original leaves us in doubt as to the kind of meat to be used, if any.

recipes.title: Fasaaninyytit
recipes.description: Paahdettu fasaani kuutioidaan ja sekoitetaan fasaanin rasvasta ja leikkeistä tehtyyn taikinaan; nyytit haudutetaan kalakastikkeella maustetussa vedessä.
instructions: Paahda fasaani kevyesti, kuutioi rintaliha ja jauha loppu liha nahan ja rasvan kanssa tahnaksi.
Sekoita kuutiot, tahna, muna, pippuri, puolet kalakastikkeesta ja viini ja muotoile nyyteiksi lusikalla.
Hauduta nyytit vedessä, jota on maustettu lopulla kalakastikkeella.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: [lightly roast choice] fresh pheasants [cut them into dice and mix these with a] stiff forcemeat made of the fat and the trimmings of the pheasant, season with pepper, broth and reduced wine, shape into croquettes or spoon dumplings, and poach in hydrogarum [water seasoned with garum, or even plain salt water].

recipes.title: Nyytit maustetussa liemessä (hydrogarata)
recipes.description: Pippurilla, lipstikalla ja hiukan bertramilla maustettu kalakastikeliemi, jossa haudutetaan lihanyytit – liemi juodaan pöydässä.
instructions: Survo mausteet ja sekoita kalakastikkeeseen ja veteen. Anna maustua hetki.
Keitä lientä hieman kokoon ja siivilöi.
Hauduta nyytit liemessä kypsiksi ja tarjoa liemen kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Crush pepper, lovage and just a suspicion of pellitory, moisten with stock and well water, allow it to draw, place it in a sauce pan, boil it down, and strain. Poach your little dumplings of forcemeat in this liquor and when they are done serve in a dish for isicia, to be sipped at the table.

recipes.title: Kanapyörykät
recipes.description: Raaka kananliha, jauhot, liemi ja pippuri – yksinkertainen roomalainen pyörykkätaikina.
instructions: Jauha kananliha ja sekoita jauhoihin, liemeen ja pippuriin.
Muotoile pyöryköiksi ja keitä kypsiksi liemessä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[raw] chicken meat, 1 lb. Of darnel [1] meal, one quarter pint of stock and one half ounce of pepper.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. lolæ floris; Hum.-List. and G.-V. olei floris--virgin olive oil?--first choice flour? Goll. olive (violet?) flowers; Dann. Olive oil. The suggestion of oil is plausible because of the lack of fat in chicken meat, but the quantity--1 lb.--is out of question. Moreover, the binder would be lacking. This is found in the Torinus rendering. His lolæ floris should read lolii--from lolium--darnel rye grass or ray grass which was supposed to have intoxicating qualities, injurious to the eye sight.--Ovid and Plautus. The seeds of this grass were supposed to possess narcotic properties but recent researches have cast doubt upon this theory. A little butter, fresh cream and eggs are the proper ingredients for chicken forcemeat. Any kind of flour for binding the forcemeat would cheapen the dish. Yet some modern forcemeats (sausage) contain as much as fifty percent of some kind of meal. The most effective is that of the soya bean which is not starchy.

recipes.title: Kanaliemi rypälemehulla
recipes.originalTitle: Chicken broth another style (ALITER DE PULLO)
recipes.description: Kananlihaa, 31 murskattua pippurinjyvää, garumia, keitettyä rypälemehua ja vettä hiljaa haihdutettuna.
instructions: Laita kaikki kattilaan ja kuumenna.
Anna hautua hiljalleen ja haihtua noin puoleen, kunnes liemi on täyteläistä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Chicken meat, 31 peppercorns crushed, 1 choenix [1] full of the very best stock, a like amount of boiled must and eleven measures [2] of water. [put this in a sauce pan] place it upon the fire to seeth and evaporate slowly.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] V. 2 sextarii; Tor. ch{oe}nicem, cenlicem; List. calicem. [2] ch{oe}nices?--left in doubt. This seems to be a chicken broth, or essence for a sauce or perhaps a medicine. Torinus mentions the chicken meat, the others do not. The original without interruption continues to describe the isicium simplex which has nothing to do with the above.

recipes.title: Lihanyytit sellerilliemessä
recipes.description: Yksi osa garumia seitsemään osaan vettä, vihreää selleriä ja pippuria – liemessä keitetään makkaratäyte tai nyytit.
instructions: Sekoita kalakastike, vesi, selleri ja pippuri ja kiehauta.
Keitä nyytit liemessä kypsiksi ja tarjoa liemen kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
To 1 acetabulum [1] of stock [2] add 7 of water, a little green celery, a little spoonful of ground pepper, and boil this with the sausage meat or dumplings. If you intend taking this to move the bowels the sediment salts [3] of hydrogarum have to be added [4].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] A measure, 15 Attic drachms. [2] liquamen. [3] Tor. pectines, alias peces hydrogaro conditi; List. sales; G.-V. fæces. [4] V. The formula is unintelligible, like No. 52 and others, perhaps just another example of medicinal cookery, dishes not only intended to nourish the body but to cure also certain ills. Authors like Hannah Wolley (The Queen-like Closet, London, 1675) and as late as the middle of the 18th century pride themselves in giving such quasi-Apician formulæ.

recipes.title: Pataruoka paksussa mausteliemessä (isicia amulata)
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, oreganoa, ripaus asafetidaa ja inkivääriä hunajan ja garumin kanssa; liemessä kypsennetään pyörykät ja kastike suurustetaan.
instructions: Sekoita mausteet, hunaja, kalakastike ja liemi kattilassa ja kiehauta.
Lisää pyörykät ja kypsennä hyvin.
Suurusta lopuksi veteen sekoitetulla jauholla ripotellen ja pohjasta sekoittaen.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Ground pepper, lovage, origany, very little silphium, a pinch of ginger and a trifle of honey and a little stock. [put on the fire, and when boiling] add the isicia [sausage, meat balls and so forth] to this broth and cook thoroughly. Finally thicken the gravy with roux [2] by sowing it in slowly and stirring from the bottom up [3].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. multa ab alieno; Brandt [a]mul[a]ta ab aheno; List. amylata--French: liés. Ab aheno--out of the pot. [2] French, for a mixture of wheat or rice flour with fats or liquids to thicken fluids. Amylum, or amulum which hereafter will occur frequently in the original does not cover the ground as well as the French term roux. The quality of the "binder" depends upon the material in hand. Sometimes the fat and flour are parched, sometimes they are used raw. Sometimes the flour is diluted with water and used in that form. [3] List. and G.-V. sorbendum; Tor. subruendum.

recipes.title: Paksu pippuri-kvittenikastike
recipes.description: Yön yli liotettu pippuri survotaan tahnaksi, ja makeutta tuo kokoon keitetty kvittenimehu tai viikunasiirappi; suurustetaan riisijauholla.
ingredients: 2 dl kvitteni- tai omenamehua keitettynä puoleen
instructions: Survo liotettu pippuri ja kalakastike tahnaksi.
Lisää keitetty kvittenimehu (tai viikunasiirappi) ja liemi.
Suurusta riisijauholla ja hauduta miedolla lämmöllä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Grind pepper which has been soaked overnight, add some more stock and work it into a smooth paste; thereupon add quince-apple cider, boiled down one half, that is which has evaporated in the heat of the sun to the consistency of honey. If this is not at hand, add fig wine [1] concentrate which the romans call "color" [2]. Now thicken the gravy with roux or with soaked rice flour and finish it on a gentle fire.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. cammarum, which should read caricarum--wine of Carica figs. [2] V. the Roman equivalent for "singe," "monkey," "Affe,"--(the vulgo French is literally translated into and in actual use in other languages) caramel color made of burnt sugar to give gravies a palatable appearance. Cf. No. 73. The reference by the original to "which the Romans call 'color'" indicates, according to Brandt, that this formula is NOT of ROMAN origin but probably a translation into Latin from a Greek cookery book. This is an interesting suggestion, and it could be elaborated on to say that the entire Apicius is NOT of Roman origin. But why should the Greeks who in their balmy days were so far in advance of Rome in culinary matters go there for such information? It is more likely that this reference to Rome comes from the Italian provinces or the colonies, regions which naturally would look to Rome for guidance in such matters.

recipes.title: Kanapata purjolla ja tillillä, riisillä suurustettuna
recipes.description: Luuton kana haudutetaan purjon, tillin ja suolan kanssa, maustetaan pippurilla ja sellerinsiemenillä ja sakeutetaan riisillä.
instructions: Hauduta kanapalat pataan purjon, tillin, suolan ja liemen kanssa kypsiksi.
Mausta pippurilla ja sellerinsiemenillä, sakeuta riisillä ja lisää kalakastike ja loraus makeaa viiniä.
Sekoita hyvin ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Disjoint a chicken and bone it. Place the pieces in a stew pan with leeks, dill and salt [water or stock] when well done add pepper and celery seed, thicken with rice [1] add stock, a dash of raisin wine or must, stir well, serve with the entrées.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] G.-V. oryzam; Tor. ditto (and on margin) oridam; Hum. oridiam legendum orindam--a kind of bread. Dann. and Goll. rice flour. In a general way the ancient formula corresponds exactly to our present chicken fricassée.

recipes.title: Speltti- tai mannavanukas pähkinöillä ja rusinoilla (apothermum)
recipes.description: Speltti keitetään pinjansiementen ja kuorittujen mantelien kanssa, lisätään rusinat ja makea viini; päälle murusia.
instructions: Keitä speltti vedessä pinjansiementen ja mantelien kanssa pehmeäksi.
Lisää rusinat ja makea viini.
Tarjoa pyöreässä kulhossa murskatut pähkinät tai murut pinnalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Boil spelt with [tor. Pignolia] nuts and peeled almonds [1] [g.-v. And] immersed in [boiling] water and washed with white clay so that they appear perfectly white, add raisins, [flavor with] condensed wine or raisin wine and serve it in a round dish with crushed [2] [nuts, fruit, bread or cake crumbs] sprinkled over it [3].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] V. We peel almonds in the same manner; the white clay treatment is new to us. G.-V. and--which is confusing. [2] The original: confractum--crushed, but what? G.-V. pepper, for which there is neither authority nor reason. A wine sauce would go well with it or crushed fruit. List. and Goll. Breadcrumbs. [3] This is a perfectly good pudding--one of the very few desserts in Apicius. With a little sweetening (supplied probably by the condensed wine) and some grated lemon for flavor it is quite acceptable as a dessert.

recipes.title: Porsasmakkara purjolla ja kuminalla
recipes.originalTitle: A dish of sow's matrix (VULVULÆ BOTELLI)
recipes.description: Hienonnettu porsaanliha survotaan pippurin, kuminan, purjon ja ruudan kanssa, lisätään pippurinjyvät ja pinjansiemenet ja keitetään suolessa purjo-tilliliemessä.
instructions: Survo pippuri, kumina ja hienonnettu purjo, lisää ruuta ja kalakastike.
Sekoita jauhelihaan, lisää kokonaiset pippurit ja pinjansiemenet ja täytä suolet.
Keitä makkarat vedessä, johon on lisätty öljyä, loraus kalakastiketta, purjo ja tilli.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Entrées [2] of sow's matrix [3] are made thus: crush pepper and cumin with two small heads of leek, peeled, add to this pulp rue, broth [and the sow's matrix or fresh pork] chop, [or crush in mortar very fine] then add to this [forcemeat] incorporating well pepper grains and [pine] nuts [4] fill the casing [5] and boil in water [with] oil and broth [for seasoning] and a bunch of leeks and dill.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] G.-V. Vulvulæ Botelli; Sch. Vulvulæ isiciata; Tor. De Vulvulis et botellis. See note No. 3. [2] V. "Entrées" out of respect for the ancients who used them as such; today we would class such dishes among the "hors d'{oe}uvres chauds." [3] V. Vulvula, dim. for vulva, sow's matrix. Cf. vulva in dictionary. Possible, also possible that volva is meant--a meat roll, a croquette. [4] V. Combinations of chopped nuts and pork still in vogue today; we use the green pistachios. [5] V. The casings which were filled with this forcemeat may have been the sow's matrices, also caul. The original is vague on the point.

recipes.title: Munamakkara pinjansiemenillä (botellum)
recipes.description: Kovaksi keitetyt keltuaiset, pinjansiemenet, sipuli ja purjo täytetään suoleen ja keitetään liemessä ja viinissä.
instructions: Murskaa keltuaiset ja sekoita pinjansiemeniin, sipuliin, purjoon ja pippuriin.
Täytä suolet.
Keitä makkarat liemen ja viinin seoksessa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Botellum is made of [2] hard boiled yolks of egg [3] chopped pignolia nuts, onion and leeks, raw ground pine [4] fine pepper, stuff in casings and cook in broth and wine [5].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] V. Botelli, or botuli, are sausage of various kind; (French, Boudin, English, Pudding). Originally made of raw blood, they are in fact, miniature blood sausage. The absence of meat in the present formula makes me believe that it is not complete, though hard boiled yolk when properly seasoned and mixed with the right amount of fat, make a tasty forcemeat for sausage. [2] Tor. Botellum sic fades ex oui; Sch. and G.-V. sex ovi--the number of eggs is immaterial. [3] Dann. Calf's Sweetbreads. [4] Goll. Thus crudum--raw blood. Thus or tus is either frankincense or the herb, ground-pine. Dann. Rosemary. Hum. Thus crudum lege jus crudum--jus or broth which would make the forcemeat soft. There is no reason for changing "thus" into "jus!" [5] G.-V. Adicies liquamen et vinum, et sic coques. Tor. & vino decoquas.

recipes.title: Lucanialainen makkara (lucanicae)
recipes.description: Pippurilla, kuminalla, kyntelillä, ruudalla, persiljalla ja laakerinmarjoilla maustettu savustettu porsasmakkara – nykyisen luganega-makkaran esi-isä.
instructions: Survo mausteet ja yrtit kalakastikkeen kanssa.
Sekoita jauhelihaan hyvin, lisää kokonaiset pippurit ja pinjansiemenet.
Täytä suolet huolellisesti ja ripusta savustumaan (tai savusta savustuspöntössä). Paista tai grillaa ennen tarjoilua.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Lucanian sausage [or meat pudding] are made similar to the above: crush pepper, cumin, savory, rue, parsley, condiment, laurel berries and broth; mix with finely chopped [fresh pork] and pound well with broth. To this mixture, being rich, add whole pepper and nuts. When filling casings carefully push the meat through. Hang sausage up to smoke.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. Lister's interesting remarks about the makers of these sausages are given in the dictionary. Cf. Longano.

recipes.title: Aivomakkara
recipes.description: Raakoja munia ja keitettyjä aivoja, pinjansiemeniä, pippuria, garumia ja ripaus asafetidaa suoleen; ryöpätään ja paistetaan.
instructions: Survo aivot ja munat sekaisin, lisää pinjansiemenet, pippurit, kalakastike ja asafetida.
Täytä suolet, ryöppää makkarat ja paista ne öljyssä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pound eggs and brains [eggs raw, brains cooked] pine nuts [chopped fine] pepper [whole] broth and a little laser with which fill the casings. First parboil the sausage then fry them and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. The directions are vague enough, but one may recognize in them our modern brain sausage.

recipes.title: Speltti-porsasmakkara sinapin kanssa
recipes.description: Keitetty speltti ja hienonnettu porsaanliha survotaan pippurin, garumin ja pinjansiementen kanssa; ryöpätään, paistetaan ja tarjotaan sinapin kanssa.
instructions: Sekoita speltti, jauheliha, pippuri, kalakastike ja pinjansiemenet.
Täytä suolet ja ryöppää makkarat.
Paista suolalla ja tarjoa sinapin kanssa – tai leikkaa viipaleiksi pyöreälle vadille.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Work cooked spelt and finely chopped fresh pork together, pound it with pepper, broth and pignolia nuts. Fill the casings, parboil and fry with salt, serve with mustard, or you may cut the sausage in slices and serve on a round dish.

recipes.title: Speltti-pekonimakkara purjolla
recipes.description: Liemessä keitetty speltti, hienonnettu rasva, purjo, pekoni ja porsaanliha sekä munat, lipstikka ja pinjansiemenet suoleen.
instructions: Keitä speltti liemessä kypsäksi ja jäähdytä.
Sekoita purjo, pekoni ja jauheliha speltin kanssa.
Survo pippuri, lipstikka ja munat ja sekoita täytteeseen pinjansiementen, kokonaisten pippurien ja kalakastikkeen kanssa.
Täytä suolet, ryöppää ja paista kevyesti – tai tarjoa keitettyinä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Wash spelt and cook it with stock. Cut the fat of the intestines or belly very fine with leeks. Mix this with chopped bacon and finely chopped fresh pork. Crush pepper, lovage and three eggs and mix all in the mortar with pignolia nuts and whole pepper, add broth, fill casings. Parboil sausage, fry lightly, or serve them boiled.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

Tor. and Tac. Serve with pheasant gravy. In the early editions the following formula which thus ends is wanting.

recipes.title: Savustetut makkararenkaat kuminakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Makkaratäyte suoleen pieniksi renkaiksi, savustetaan punertaviksi, paistetaan ja tarjotaan kuminalla maustetun viinikastikkeen päällä.
instructions: Täytä suolet ja muotoile pieniksi renkaiksi. Savusta, kunnes ne saavat punertavan värin (tai käytä valmiita savumakkaroita).
Paista renkaat kevyesti.
Keitä kastikkeen aineet kokoon, suurusta ja asettele renkaat kastikkeen päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Fill the casings with the best material [forcemeat] shape the sausage into small circles, smoke. When they have taken on (vermillion) color fry them lightly. Dress nicely garnished on a pheasant wine gravy, flavored, however, with cumin.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

V. In Tor. and in the earliest edition this formula has been contracted with the preceding and made one formula.

recipes.title: Vihannekset vihreiksi
recipes.description: Roomalainen niksi: vihannekset pysyvät vihreinä, kun ne keitetään ruokasoodan kanssa.
instructions: Keitä vihannekset vedessä, johon on lisätty ripaus soodaa – ne pysyvät kirkkaanvihreinä. (Nykytiedolla sooda tosin pehmentää ja vie vitamiineja.)
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
To keep all vegetables green. Ut omne holus smaragdinum fiat.

All vegetables will remain green if boiled with cooking soda [1].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Nitrium. Method still in use today, considered injurious to health if copper vessel is used, but the amount of copper actually absorbed by the vegetable is infinitesimal, imperceptible even by the taste. Copper, to be actually harmful would have to be present in such quantity as to make enjoyment impossible.

recipes.title: Punajuuret ja purjot pippuri-kuminaliemessä
recipes.originalTitle: Vegetable dinner, easily digested (PULMENTARIUM AD VENTREM)
recipes.description: Nuoret punajuuret ja purjot ryöpätään, asetellaan vuokaan ja kypsennetään pippurin, kuminan, garumin ja rypälesiirapin kanssa.
instructions: Ryöppää kuoritut punajuuret ja purjot ja asettele ne vuokaan.
Sekoita pippuri, kumina, kalakastike, siirappi ja vesi ja kaada päälle.
Kypsennä miedolla lämmöllä pehmeiksi ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
All green vegetables are suited for this purpose [2] very young [3] beets and well matured leeks are parboiled; arrange them in a baking dish, grind pepper and cumin, add broth and condensed must, or anything else to sweeten them a little, heat and finish them on a slow fire, and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] V. Ad ventrem, "for the belly," simple home laxative. [2] V. This sentence in Torinus only. Possibly a contraction of the foregoing formula, No. 66. [3] V. minutas, "small," i.e., young.

recipes.title: Mangoldinipput kuminalla ja pähkinöillä
recipes.description: Mangoldi sidotaan nippuihin ja keitetään, maustetaan rypälesiirapilla ja kuminalla, ja lopuksi kuumaan pannuun lisätään pähkinät ja garum.
instructions: Pese mangoldi, sido nipuiksi ja keitä pehmeäksi.
Mausta siirapilla ja kuminalla, ripottele pippuria ja lisää öljy.
Survo pähkinät kalakastikkeen kanssa, lisää kuumaan pannuun mangoldin joukkoon, nosta liedeltä ja tarjoa heti.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Scrub and wash bundles of beets by rubbing them with a little soda [2]. Tie them in individual bundles, put into water to be cooked, when done, season with reduced must or raisin wine and cumin, sprinkle with pepper, add a little oil, and when hot, crush polypody and nuts with broth, add this to the red-hot pan, incorporating it with the beets, take off the fire quickly and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] This formula wanting in Tor. [2] V. Ingenious method to skin tender root vegetables, still in vogue today. We remove the skin of tender young root vegetables, carrots, beets, etc., by placing them in a towel, sprinkling them with rock salt and shaking them energetically. The modern power vegetable peeler is really built on the same principle, only instead of salt (which soon melts) carborundum or rough concrete surfaces are used, against which surfaces the vegetables are hurled by the rotary motion; often enough, too much of the skin is removed, however.

recipes.title: Varron punajuuret simassa
recipes.description: Mustat punajuuret keitetään hunajavedessä suolan ja öljyn kanssa, kunnes liemi imeytyy juuriin; liemi on hyvä juoma. Samassa voi keittää kanan.
instructions: Puhdista punajuuret huolellisesti.
Keitä ne hunajavedessä suolan ja öljyn kanssa, kunnes liemi on haihtunut ja imeytynyt juuriin.
Ohjeen mukaan samassa liemessä voi keittää myös kanan.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Varro beets, that is, black ones [2] of which the roots must be cleaned well, cook them with mead and a little salt and oil; boil them down in this liquor so that the roots are saturated thereby; the liquid itself is good drinking. It is also nice to cook a chicken in with them.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] G.-V. Betacios; Tor. B. Varrones. Probably named for Varro, the writer on agriculture. [2] Roots on the order of parsnips, salsify, oysterplant.

recipes.title: Selleri pippuri-hunajakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Keitetty selleri ja purjo; keitinlieme survotaan pippurin, garumin ja hunajan kanssa kastikkeeksi sellerin päälle.
instructions: Keitä selleri ja purjon vaalea osa vedessä, kunnes vettä on jäljellä kaksi kolmannesta.
Survo pippuri, kalakastike ja hunaja ja sekoita keitinliemeen. Siivilöi ja keitä uudelleen.
Kaada kastike keitetyn sellerin päälle; lisää halutessasi viipaloitua sellerinjuurta.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Another vegetable dish, promoting good health; wash celery, greens and roots, and dry it in the sun: then also cook the tender part and head of leeks in a new [1] pot, allowing the water to boil down one third of its volume. Thereupon grind pepper with broth and honey in equal amounts properly measured, mix it in the mortar with the water of the cooked celery, strain, boil again and use it to mask the [cooked] celery with. If desired, add [the sliced root of the] celery to it [2].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] V. "new," i.e., cook leeks in a separate sauce pan; NOT together with the celery, which, as the original takes for granted, must be cooked also. [2] V. We would leave the honey out, make a cream sauce from the stock, or, adding bouillon, tie same with a little flour and butter, and would call the dish Stewed Celery and Leeks. The ancient method is entirely rational because the mineral salts of the vegetables are preserved and utilized (invariably observed by Apicius) which today are often wasted by inexperienced cooks who discard these precious elements with the water in which vegetables are boiled.

recipes.title: Parsa
recipes.description: Kuorittu ja kuivattu parsa upotetaan kiehuvaan veteen latvat ylöspäin.
instructions: Kuori ja pese parsat ja kuivaa ne.
Seisota parsat kiehuvassa suolavedessä tyvet alaspäin niin, että latvat höyrystyvät, ja keitä kypsiksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Asparagus [tor. In order to have it most agreeable to the palate] must be [peeled, washed and] dried [1] and immersed in boiling water backwards [2] [3].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] V. Must be dried before boiling because the cold water clinging to the stalks is likely to chill the boiling water too much in which the asparagus is to be cooked. Apicius here reveals himself as the consummate cook who is familiar with the finest detail of physical and chemical changes which food undergoes at varying temperatures. The various editions all agree: asparagos siccabis; Schuch, however, says: "For the insane siccabis I substitute siciabis, isiciabis, prepare with sicio [?] and cook." He even goes on to interpret it cucabis from the Greek kouki, cocoanut milk, and infers that the asparagus was first cooked in cocoanut milk and then put back into water, a method we are tempted to pronounce insane. [2] V. Backwards! G.-V. rursum in calidam; Tac. rursus in aquam calidam; Tor. ac rursus ... This word has caused us some reflection, but the ensuing discovery made it worth while. Rursus has escaped the attention of the other commentators. In this case rursus means backwards, being a contraction from revorsum, h.e. reversum. The word is important enough to be observed. Apicius evidently has the right way of cooking the fine asparagus. The stalks, after being peeled and washed must be bunched together and tied according to sizes, and the bunches must be set into the boiling water "backwards," that is, they must stand upright with the heads protruding from the water. The heads will be made tender above the water line by rising steam and will be done simultaneously with the harder parts of the stalks. We admit, we have never seen a modern cook observe this method. They usually boil the tender heads to death while the lower stalks are still hard. Though this formula is incomplete (it fails to state the sauce to be served, also that the asparagus must be peeled and bunched, that the water must contain salt, etc.) it is one of the neatest formulæ in Apicius. It is amusing to note how the author herein unconsciously reveals what a poor litérateur but what a fine cook he is. This is characteristic of most good practitioners. One may perfectly master the vast subject of cookery, yet one may not be able to give a definition of even a single term, let alone the ability to exactly describe one of the many processes of cookery. Real poets often are in the same predicament; none of them ever explained the art satisfactorily. [3] G.-V. add to the formula callosiores reddes--give back [eliminate] the harder ones. This sentence belongs to the next article. And Torinus, similar to Humelbergius, renders this sentence ut reddas ad gustum calliores--to render the harder ones palatable--the squash and pumpkin namely--and we are inclined to agree with him.

recipes.title: Kurpitsa pippuri-kumina-etikkaliemessä
recipes.description: Keitetty kurpitsa vuokaan; päälle survottua pippuria, kuminaa, asafetidaa ja ruutaa garumin, etikan ja keitetyn viinin kanssa, kiehautetaan kolmesti.
instructions: Keitä kurpitsapalat, purista vesi pois ja asettele vuokaan.
Survo mausteet ja sekoita kalakastikkeeseen, etikkaan ja siirappiin. Siivilöi ja kaada kurpitsan päälle.
Kiehauta kolme kertaa, nosta liedeltä ja ripottele päälle vähän pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
To have the harder ones palatable, do this: [1] [cut the fruit into pieces, boil and] squeeze the water out of the boiled fruit and arrange [the pieces] in a baking dish. Put in the mortar pepper, cumin and silphium, that is, a very little of the laser root and a little rue, season this with stock, measure a little vinegar and mix in a little condensed wine, so that it can be strained [2] and pour this liquid over the fruit in the baking dish; let it boil three times, retire from the fire and sprinkle with very little ground pepper.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Cf. note 3 to No. 72. [2] List. Ut coloretur--to give it color; Tor. ut ius coletur--from colo--to strain, to filter. Cf. also note 2 to No. 55.

recipes.title: Kurpitsa taron tapaan
recipes.originalTitle: Pumpkin like dasheens (ALITER CUCURBITAS IURE COLOCASIORUM)
recipes.description: Keitetty kurpitsa kypsennetään loppuun pippuri-kumina-ruutaliemessä, joka suurustetaan; päälle pippuria.
instructions: Keitä kurpitsa ja purista vesi pois.
Survo pippuri, kumina ja ruuta, lisää etikka, kalakastike ja vesi ja kiehauta.
Lisää kurpitsat ja kypsennä, suurusta liemi. Ripottele pippuria ennen tarjoilua.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Boil the pumpkin in water like colocasia; grind pepper, cumin and rue, add vinegar and measure out the broth in a saucepan.
