recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Eel will be made more palatable by a sauce which has [1] pepper, celery seed, lovage [2], anise, syrian sumach [3], figdate wine [4], honey, vinegar, broth, oil, mustard, reduced must.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Tor. sentence wanting in other texts. [2] Note the position of lovage in this formula. Usually it follows pepper. We have finally accounted for this peculiarity. Torinus, throughout the original, treats "pepper" and "lovage" as one spice, whereas we have kept the two separate. He believed it to be a certain kind of pepper--piper Ligusticum. Piper, as a matter of fact, stands for pepper, and Ligusticum is the herb, Lovage, an umbelliferous plant, also called Levisticum. The fact that the two words are here separated plainly shows that Torinus has been in the dark about this matter almost to the end. One wonders why he did not change or correct this error in the preceding books. His marginal errata prove that his work was being printed as he wrote it, or furnished copy therefor--namely in installments. Since the printer's type was limited, each sheet was printed in the complete edition, and the type was then used over again for the next sheet. [3] Tor. thun. [4] Wanting in Tor.

recipes.title: Ankerias keltuais-sumakkikastikkeessa
recipes.originalTitle: Another sauce for eel (ALITER IUS IN ANGUILLAM)
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, sumakkia, kuivattua minttua, ruudanmarjoja ja kovaksi keitettyjä keltuaisia siman, etikan, garumin ja öljyn kanssa keitettynä – kirjan kymmenennen kirjan viimeinen ohje.
instructions: Grillaa tai paista kala öljyllä siveltynä.
Survo kastikkeen mausteet ja sekoita nesteet joukkoon. Keitä hetki ja kaada kalan päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pepper, lovage, syrian sumach, dry mint, rue berries, hard yolks, mead, vinegar, broth, oil; cook it.

_

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

THE EXCERPTS FROM APICIUS BY VINIDARIUS THE ILLUSTRIOUS MAN [1] Pigmentorum--specierum--spices. The old pigmentum is really any coloring matter; the word, corrupted to pimento and pimiento is now used for sweet red pepper and also for allspice. [2] Cariofilu--cærefolium--Chærephyllon; Fr. Cerfeuille; Ger. Kerbel. This should be among the herbs. [3] Not identified. [1] Not identified. Perhaps the seed of thyme, though the word bacas would be out of place there. [2] Ospera, i.e., Osperios. [3] Samsucu, i.e., sampsuchum Elderberries? [4] Not identified; perhaps laurus innubus, dried virgin laurel leaves. [1] Not identified. We take it to be honey mead, or some other honey preparation, maybe, piperatum, pepper sauce. [1] Acmidula, i.e., amygdala. [2] Aballana--abellana--abellinæ--avellana; Fr. avelline. I. CASSEROLE OF VEGETABLES AND CHICKEN CACCABINA MINORE II. STUFFED CHARTREUSE CACCABINA FUSILE III. BRAISED CUTLETS OFELLAS GARATAS IV. ROAST MEAT BALLS OFELLAS ASSAS V. GLAZED CUTLETS ALITER OFELLAS VI. MEAT BALLS WITH LASER OFELLAS GRATON VII. SEA SCORPION WITH TURNIPS PISCES SCORPIONES RAPULATAS VIII. ANY KIND OF FISH, FRIED PISCES FRIXOS CUIUSCUMQUE GENERIS IX. FRIED FISH ITEM PISCES FRIXOS X. ROAST [Grilled] FISH PISCES ASSOS XI. FRIED FISH AND WINE SAUCE PISCES INOTOGONON XII. SARDINES, BABY TUNNY, WHITING SARDAS XIII. FISH STEWED IN WINE ITEM PISCES INOTOGONON XIV. STEWED MULLET WITH DILL MULLOS ANETATOS XV. MULLET, DIFFERENT STYLE ALITER MULLOS XVI. MURENA AND EEL MURENAS ET ANGUILLAS XVII. SPINY LOBSTER AND SQUILL LUCUSTAS ET ISQUILLAS XVIII. BOILED FISH PISCES ELIXOS XIX. A DISH OF SOLE AND EGGS PATINAS OBORUM XX. SUCKLING PIG, CORIANDER SAUCE PORCELLO CORIANDRATU XXI. SUCKLING PIG, WINE SAUCE PORCELLO IN OCCUCTU XXII. PORK, PAN GRAVY PORCELLO EO IURE XXIII. PORK SPRINKLED WITH THYME PORCELLO TYMMO CRAPSU XXIV. PICKLED PORK PORCELLU EXOZOME XXV. LASER [sauce for] PORK PORCELLU LASARATU XXVI. SAUCE FOR PORK PORCELLU IUSCELLU XXVII. PLAIN LAMB AGNU SIMPLICE XXVIII. KID AND LASER HEDU LASARATU XXIX. THRUSH, HEALTH STYLE TURDOS APONTOMENUS XXX. TURTLEDOVES TURTURES XXXI. SAUCE FOR PARTRIDGE IUS IN PERDICES [1] Brevis cyboru could be nicely and appropriately rendered with "Menu,"--something minute, short,--but this list is not a menu in our modern sense. It is an enumeration of recipe names, a summary of dishes contained in the excerpts. There is considerable variation in the spelling of the names here and in the following. Syllables ending with "u" are invariably abbreviations of "um."

recipes.title: Vihannes-kanavuoka (caccabina minor)
recipes.originalTitle: A casserole of vegetable and chicken (CACCABINAM MINOREM)
recipes.description: Kypsiä vihanneksia ja kanaa vuokaan, garumia ja öljyä; päälle pippurista, laakerista ja munasta tehty seos, joka painetaan tiiviiksi.
instructions: Kerrosta vihannekset ja kana vuokaan, lisää kalakastike ja öljy ja kiehauta.
Survo pippuri ja laakeri, sekoita munaan ja kaada vuokaan.
Paina tiiviiksi ja kypsennä uunissa 175 asteessa noin 20 minuuttia.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Arrange different kinds of cooked vegetables in a casserole with [cooked] chicken interspersed, if you like; season with broth and oil, set to boil. Next crush a little pepper and leaves, and mix an egg in with the dressing [add this to the vegetables] press [into the casserole, eliminating the juice] [2].

Ia

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] The dish resembles a chartreuse. [2] Juice should be extracted before the addition of the egg, if the dish is to be unmoulded.

recipes.title: Kaalivuoka kirvelillä ja laakerilla
recipes.originalTitle: The same, with another dressing, a cabbage _chartreuse_ (ALIAS: TRITURA UNDE PERFUNDES CACCABINAM)
recipes.description: Keitetty kaali survotaan kirvelin, laakerin ja korianterinlehtien kanssa, kypsennetään vuoassa höyryssä, kumotaan ja tarjotaan maustetun kastikkeen päällä.
instructions: Survo kaali ja yrtit ja sekoita munat joukkoon.
Painele voideltuun vuokaan ja kypsennä vesihauteessa noin 30 minuuttia.
Kumoa vadille, koristele ja kaada kastike alle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush whatever quantity of leaves is required with chervil and one and a quarter part of laurel berries, a medium-sized boiled cabbage, coriander leaves, dissolve with its own juice, steam in the hot ashes, but first place in a mould [when stiff unmould on a platter] decorate, pour under a well-seasoned sauce, and so serve [1].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Either the vegetables and chicken of {Rx} No. 468 are combined with this dressing or a purée of the above cabbage, etc., is made, which will make this an integral dish. The instructions are vague enough to leave room for this choice; but there can be no doubt but what we have here a formula for a vegetable purée or a pudding, a genuine "Chartreuse," such as were prepared in the fancy moulds so popular in old Rome. The "Chartreuse," then, is not original with the vegetarian monks of the monastery by that name, the Carthusians.

recipes.title: Täytetty kerrosvuoka (caccabina fusilis)
recipes.description: Kypsiä vihanneksia, kanapyöryköitä ja porsaanpaloja kerroksittain vuokaan; päälle pippuria ja lipstikkaa vanhan viinin, garumin, hunajan ja öljyn kanssa ja munilla sidottuna.
ingredients: 300 g kypsiä vihanneksia (malva, purjo, punajuuri, kaalinversot)
instructions: Kerrosta vihannekset ja lihat vuokaan.
Survo mausteet ja sekoita viiniin, kalakastikkeeseen, hunajaan ja öljyyn; maista ja vatkaa munat joukkoon.
Kaada vuokaan ja paista 175 asteessa noin 30 minuuttia.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[take cooked] mallows, leeks, beets, or cooked cabbage sprouts [shoots or tender strunks] thrushes [roast] and quenelles of chicken, tidbits of pork or squab chicken and other similar shreds of fine meats that may be available; arrange everything alternately in layers [in a mould or in a casserole]. Crush pepper and lovage with 2 parts of old wine, 1 part broth, 1 part honey and a little oil. Taste it; and when well mixed and in due proportions put in a sauce pan and allow to heat moderately; when boiling add a pint of milk in which [about eight] eggs have been dissolved; [next] pour [this spiced custard] over [the layers of vegetables and meats, heat slowly without allowing to boil] and when congealed serve [either in the casserole, or carefully unmould the dish on a service platter] [2].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] It is interesting to note how the generic terms, salacaccabia and caccabina have degenerated here. In these formulas the terms have lost all resemblance to the former meaning, the original "salt meat boiled in a pot." Such changes are very often observed in the terminology of our modern kitchens, in every language. They make the definition of terms and the classification of subjects extremely difficult. They add much to the confusion among cooks and guests in public dining places and create misunderstandings that only an expert can explain. [2] This dish affords an opportunity for a decorative scheme by the arrangement of the various vegetables and meats in a pleasing and artistic manner, utilizing the various colors and shapes of the bits of food as one would use pieces of stone in a mosaic. Of course, such a design can be appreciated only if the chartreuse is served unmoulded, i.e. if the cook succeeds in unmoulding it without damaging the structure.

recipes.title: Garumissa haudutetut lihapalat
recipes.description: Lihapalat haudutetaan yhtä suuressa määrässä garumia ja öljyä tilkan hunajaa kanssa.
instructions: Laita liha pataan kalakastikkeen, öljyn ja hunajan kanssa.
Hauduta miedolla lämmöllä kypsäksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Place the meat in a stew pan, add one pound [2] of broth, a like quantity of oil, a trifle of honey, and thus braise [3].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Derived from garum or {oe}nogarum, the wine sauce. These are supposed to be meat balls or cutlets prepared with garum, but the garum is not mentioned in the formula. This also illustrates the interesting etymology of the word. It is not recognized in every-day ancient language because it is a typical technical term, the much complained-of lingua culinaria. We find, therefore, that--at least in this instance--garum no longer stands for a sauce made from the fish, garus, but that garum has become a generic term for certain kinds of sauces. Danneil renders garatus with lasaratus, which is clearly out of place. [2] In this instance, and in several others, and also according to Sueton. Cæs. fluids were weighed. What idea could be more practical, useful and more "modern" than this? Sheer commercial greed, stubbornness, indolence have thus far made futile all efforts towards more progressive methods in handling food stuffs, particularly in the weighing of them and in selling them by their weight. Present market methods are very chaotic, and are kept purposely so to the detriment of the buyer. [3] The original: et sic frigis.--Frigo is equivalent to frying, drying, parching; the word here has taken on a broader meaning, because the "frying" process is clearly out of question here. It appears that the terminology of frigo and that of asso in the next formula, has not been clearly defined. As a matter of fact, not many modern cooks today are able to give a clear definition of such terms as frying, broiling, roasting, braising, baking, which are thus subject to various interpretations.

recipes.title: Lihapyörykät viinikastikkeessa
recipes.description: Ruskistetut lihapyörykät haudutetaan viinikastikkeessa ja tarjotaan samassa kastikkeessa pippurilla.
instructions: Ruskista pyörykät öljyssä.
Lisää viini ja kalakastike ja hauduta kypsiksi. Ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Meatballs [previously sauté], carefully prepared, arrange in a shallow stew pan and braise them in wine sauce; afterwards serve them in the same sauce or gravy, sprinkled with pepper.

recipes.title: Hunajakuorrutetut lihapalat
recipes.description: Lihapalat haudutetaan garumissa ja kuorrutetaan kuumalla hunajalla.
instructions: Hauduta liha liemessä ja kalakastikkeessa kypsäksi.
Kuumenna hunaja ja kääntele lihapalat siinä kiiltäviksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The meat pieces are braised [1] in broth and are glazed [2] with hot honey [3] and thus served.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Cf. note 3 to Excerpta III. [2] unguantur. [3] Dann. oil; G.-V. melle--honey. It is quite common to use honey for glazing foods. Today we sprinkle meats (ham) with sugar, exposing it to the open heat to melt it; the sugar thus forms a glaze or crust.

recipes.title: Inkivääri-kardemummapyörykät
recipes.description: Lihapyörykät kypsennetään asafetidan, inkiväärin, kardemumman ja tilkan garumia seoksessa.
instructions: Sekoita mausteet, kalakastike ja vesi pannulla.
Kypsennä pyörykät seoksessa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Laser, ginger, cardamom, and a dash of broth; crush this all, mix well, and cook the meat ball therein [2].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Cf. Summary of Dishes, and note 1 to Excerpta III. [2] Dann. adds cumin, due perhaps to the faulty reading of the sentence, misces cum his omnibus tritis, etc.

recipes.title: Simppu nauriiden ja sahramin kanssa
recipes.description: Kala haudutetaan garumissa ja öljyssä; joukkoon hienonnettu keitetty nauris ja runsaasti öljyä, mausteena kumina, laakeri ja sahrami; sakeutetaan riisijauholla.
instructions: Hauduta kala kalakastikkeessa ja öljyssä puolikypsäksi.
Hienonna nauris, purista kuivaksi ja lisää kalan joukkoon runsaan öljyn kanssa.
Survo kumina, laakeri ja sahrami, lisää pataan ja sakeuta riisijauholla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cook [the fish] in broth and oil, retire when half done: soak boiled turnips, chop very fine and squeeze them in your hands so that they have no more moisture in them; then combine them with the fish and let them simmer with plenty of oil: and while this cooks, crush cumin, half of that amount of laurel berries, and, because of the color, add saffron; bind with rice flour to give it the right consistency. Add a dash of vinegar and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] rapa, rapum: white turnip, rape; "turniped."

recipes.title: Paistettu kala taateli-oreganokastikkeessa
recipes.originalTitle: [sauce for] any kind of fish, fried make thus: (PISCES FRIXOS CUIUSCUMQUE GENERIS)
recipes.description: Pippuria, korianterinsiementä, asafetidaa, oreganoa, ruutaa ja taateleita etikan, öljyn, garumin ja rypälesiirapin kanssa kuumana paistetun kalan päälle.
instructions: Käännä kala jauhoissa ja paista öljyssä.
Survo kastikkeen aineet ja kuumenna pienessä kattilassa.
Kaada kuuma kastike kalan päälle ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Crush pepper, coriander seed, laser root, origany, rue, figdates, moisten with vinegar, oil, broth, adding reduced must, all this prepare and mix carefully, place in small casserole to heat. When thoroughly heated, pour over the fried fish, sprinkle with pepper and serve.

recipes.title: Paistettu kala laakeri-korianterikastikkeessa
recipes.originalTitle: [sauce for] same fried fish make thus: (ITEM PISCES FRIXOS)
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, laakerinmarjoja ja korianteria hunajan, garumin, viinin ja makean viinin kanssa hiljalleen keitettynä ja riisijauholla sakeutettuna.
instructions: Käännä kala jauhoissa ja paista öljyssä.
Survo mausteet, lisää hunaja, kalakastike ja viinit ja keitä miedolla lämmöllä.
Sakeuta riisijauholla ja tarjoa kalan kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush pepper, lovage [1], laurel berries, coriander, and moisten with honey, broth [2], wine, raisin wine, or reduced spiced wine; cook this on a slow fire, bind with rice flour and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Sch. ligisticum. [2] Wanting in Sch.

recipes.title: Paahdettu kala tilli-keltuaiskastikkeen päällä
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, kynteliä, kuivattua sipulia, taateleita, tilliä ja keltuaisia hunajan, etikan, garumin, öljyn ja rypälesiirapin kanssa kalan alle.
instructions: Paahda tai paista kala.
Survo kastikkeen aineet tasaiseksi ja levitä annoksen alle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush pepper, lovage, satury, dry onions, moisten with vinegar, add figdates, dill, yolks of egg, honey, vinegar, broth, oil, reduced must; all this mix thoroughly and underlay [the fish with it].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] The fish was probably broiled on the craticula (see our illustration). The nature of this sauce is not quite clear. If properly handled, it might turn out to be a highly seasoned mayonnaise, or a vinaigrette, depending on the mode of manipulation; either would be suitable for fried or broiled fish.

recipes.title: Paistettu kala viini-yrttikastikkeessa
recipes.description: Paistetulle kalalle kastike pippurista, lipstikasta, ruudasta, vihreistä yrteistä ja kuivatusta sipulista öljyn, viinin ja garumin kanssa.
instructions: Paista kala öljyssä.
Survo mausteet ja yrtit, sekoita öljy, viini ja kalakastike joukkoon ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Fry the fish; crush pepper, lovage, rue, green herbs, dry onions, add oil [wine] broth and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Ihm and G.-V. {oe}noteganon; inotogono and in the Summary of Dishes inotogonon; Sch. eleogaro. Rather an obscure term, owing to the diversity of spelling. We would call it a dish stewed in or prepared with wine, although wine is absent in the present formula. However, it is given in XIII, which bears the same name. Dann. is obviously mistaken in styling this preparation "oil broth."

recipes.title: Sardiinit kylmällä keltuais-oreganokastikkeella
recipes.originalTitle: [cold sauce for] sardines make thus: (SARDAS SIC FACIES)
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, oreganoa, kuivattua sipulia ja kovaksi keitettyjä keltuaisia etikan ja öljyn kanssa tasaiseksi kastikkeeksi sardiinien alle.
instructions: Paista tai grillaa sardiinit.
Survo kastikkeen aineet tasaiseksi ja levitä kalojen alle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush pepper, lovage seed, origany, dry onions, hard boiled yolks, vinegar, oil; this must be combined into one [2] and underlaid.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] A kind of small tunny, which, like our herring, used to be pickled or salt, corresponding to the anchovy. A "sardine," from the island of Sardinia; Sardus, the inhabitant of Sardinia. [2] The absence of detailed instructions as to the manipulation of the yolks, oil and vinegar is regrettable; upon them depends the certainty or uncertainty of whether the ancients had our modern mayonnaise.

recipes.title: Kalapata viinissä purjon ja korianterin kanssa
recipes.description: Kalapalat haudutetaan öljyssä, garumissa ja etikassa purjo-korianterinipun kanssa; nippu survotaan pippurin, oreganon ja lipstikan kanssa kastikkeeksi.
instructions: Laita kala kattilaan öljyn, kalakastikkeen, etikan, viinin ja yrttinippujen kanssa ja hauduta.
Survo pippuri, oregano ja lipstikka keitettyjen purjon ja korianterin kanssa ja kaada kattilaan.
Nosta kala vadille, suurusta liemi ja kaada päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Raw fish any kind you prefer, wash [prepare, cut into handy size] arrange in a sauce pan; add oil, broth, vinegar, a bunch of leeks and [fresh] coriander, and cook: [meanwhile] crush pepper, origany, lovage with the bunches of leeks and coriander which you have cooked [with the fish] and pour [this preparation] into the sauce pan. [when the fish is done, retire it and arrange the pieces in the serving dish, casserole, bowl or platter] bring the residue in the sauce pan to a boiling point, allow it to reduce slowly to the right consistency [strain the sauce of the fish] sprinkle with pepper and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Cf. note to XI. This {oe}noteganon resembles the Bouillabaisse, the famous Marseilles fish chowder. In addition to the above manner it is flavored with saffron. An excellent dish, especially with the judicious addition of onions, parsley, a suspicion of garlic and small sippets of toasted bread.

recipes.title: Tillimullot
recipes.originalTitle: Mullet stewed with dill make thus: (MULLOS ANETHATOS SIC FACIES)
recipes.description: Kala haudutetaan öljyssä, garumissa ja viinissä purjon, korianterin ja tillin kanssa; kastike pippurista, öljystä, etikasta ja makeasta viinistä suurustetaan ja kaadetaan päälle.
instructions: Hauduta kala öljyssä, kalakastikkeessa ja viinissä yrttien kanssa.
Survo pippuri, lisää öljy, etikka ja makea viini, kuumenna ja suurusta.
Kaada kastike kalan päälle ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Prepare the fish [clean, wash, trim, cut into pieces] and place in a sauce pan, adding oil, broth, wine, bunches of leeks, [fresh] coriander, [fresh dill]; place on fire to cook. [meanwhile] put pepper in the mortar, pound it, add oil, and one part of vinegar and raisin wine to taste. [this preparation] transfer into a sauce pan, place on the fire to heat, tie with roux, add to the fish in the sauce pan. Sprinkle with pepper and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] From anethus--dill--which is omitted in formula. Sch. anecatos, i.e. submersos, because the original fails to state the dill in the formula. Such conjecture is not justified.

recipes.title: Mullot oregano-lipstikkakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Kala haudutetaan öljyssä, garumissa ja viinissä purjon ja korianterin kanssa; kastike pippurista, lipstikasta ja oreganosta kalan liemellä ja makealla viinillä.
instructions: Hauduta kala öljyssä, kalakastikkeessa ja viinissä purjon ja korianterin kanssa.
Survo mausteet, kostuta kalan liemellä ja makealla viinillä, kuumenna ja suurusta.
Kaada kastike pataan ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Scrape, wash, place [the fish] in a sauce pan, add oil, broth, wine and a bunch of leeks and [fresh] coriander to the mess, set on the fire to cook. Crush pepper, lovage, origany, moisten with some of the fish's own liquor [from the sauce pan] add raisin wine to taste, put it into a pot and on the fire to heat; tie with roux and presently add it to the contents in the sauce pan [1] sprinkle with pepper and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] It appears that the patina mentioned in this and in the foregoing formula is either a finely wrought metal sauce pan or chafing dish, or a plainer cumana, an earthenware casserole; either of which may be used for service at the table. It may be noticed how this manner of preparing fish has a tendency to preserve all the savory flavors and juices of the fish, a process in this respect both rational and economical.

recipes.title: Ankerias minttu-hunajaliemessä
recipes.originalTitle: Murena, eel or mullet make thus: (MURENAM AUT ANGUILLAS VEL MULLOS SIC FACIES)
recipes.description: Kala kypsennetään kokonaan peittävässä liemessä, jossa pippuria, lipstikkaa, oreganoa, minttua ja kuivattua sipulia viinin, garumin, hunajan ja rypälesiirapin kanssa.
instructions: Asettele kala kattilaan.
Survo mausteet ja sekoita viiniin, kalakastikkeeseen, hunajaan ja siirappiin. Kaada kalan päälle niin, että se peittyy.
Hauduta kypsäksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Clean the fish and carefully place in a sauce pan. In the mortar put pepper, lovage, origany, mint, dry onions, crush, moisten with a small glass of wine, half of that of broth, and of honey one third part, and a moderate amount of reduced must, say a spoonful. It is necessary that the fish be entirely covered by this liquor so that there may be sufficient juice during the cooking.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] The ancients considered the murena one of the finest of fish; the best were brought from the straits of Sicily. Rich Romans kept them alive in their fish ponds, often large and elaborate marble basins called, piscina, fattened the fish, kept it ready for use. Pollio fattened murenas on human flesh, killing a slave on the slightest provocation and throwing the body into the fish pond; he would eat only the liver of such murenas. This is the only case of such cruelty on record, and it has often been cited and exaggerated. [2] Perhaps the sea-eel, or conger, according to Dann. Also very much esteemed. The witty Plautus names a cook in one of his comedies "Congrio," because the fellow was "slippery."

recipes.title: Langustin keltuaiskastike
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa ja sellerinsiementä etikan, garumin ja kovaksi keitettyjen keltuaisten kanssa keitetyn langustin tai ravun lihan päälle.
ingredients: 600 g keitettyä langustin-, hummerin- tai ravunlihaa
instructions: Survo mausteet ja keltuaiset etikan ja kalakastikkeen kanssa tasaiseksi.
Kääntele äyriäisten liha kastikkeessa ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush pepper, lovage, celery seed, pour in vinegar, broth, yolks of [hard boiled] eggs, mix well together [2] and dress [the boiled shellfish meat with it] and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Cf. Summary of Dishes. [2] Another of Apicii hasty and laconic formulæ. No indication as to how to use the ingredients named. According to our notion of eating, there is only one way: The shellfish is boiled in aromatic water, allowed to cool off; the meat is then taken out of the shells; the above named ingredients are combined in a manner of a mayonnaise or a vinaigrette, although the necessary oil is not mentioned here. The dressing is poured over the shellfish meat, and the result is a sort of salad or "cocktail" as we have today.

recipes.title: Keitetty kala pinjansiemen-taatelikastikkeessa
recipes.description: Pippuria, lipstikkaa, sellerinsiementä ja oreganoa etikassa; pinjansiemeniä, taateleita, hunajaa, garumia ja sinappia.
instructions: Keitä kala suolavedessä.
Survo kastikkeen aineet ja tarjoa kalan kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush pepper, lovage, celery seed, origany which moisten with vinegar; add pine nuts, figdates [1] in sufficient quantity, honey, vinegar, broth, mustard, mix and combine properly and bring forth.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Dann. is undecided as to whether this is dates or date wine; Goll. thinks it is mustard seed, which is not so bad gastronomically; but the original leaves no room for any doubt.

recipes.title: Kampelavuoka munilla
recipes.originalTitle: A dish of sole with eggs (PATINA SOLEARUM EX OVIS)
recipes.description: Kampelat haudutetaan garumissa, öljyssä ja viinissä purjon ja korianterinsiementen kanssa; liemi sekoitetaan kymmeneen munaan ja kaadetaan kalojen päälle hyytymään.
instructions: Hauduta kala matalassa pannussa kalakastikkeessa, öljyssä ja viinissä purjon ja korianterinsiementen kanssa.
Survo pippuri ja oregano kalan liemellä, vatkaa munat ja loput liemestä joukkoon.
Kaada seos kalojen päälle ja hyydytä miedolla lämmöllä keittämättä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Scale [skin] clean [the soles], place in a [shallow] sauce pan, add broth, oil [white] wine, a bunch of leeks and coriander seed, place on fire to cook, grind a little pepper, origany, moisten with the fish liquor [from the sauce pan]. Take 10 raw eggs, beat them and mix with the remaining liquor; put it all back over the fish, and on a slow fire allow to heat [without boiling] and thicken to the right consistency; sprinkle with pepper [1].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Very similar to Sole au vin blanc. Cf. {Rx} No. 155.

recipes.title: Korianteriporsas rusinoilla ja pinjansiemenillä
recipes.description: Paahdetun porsaan päälle kuuma kastike pippurista, tillistä, oreganosta ja tuoreesta korianterista hunajan, viinin, garumin, öljyn, etikan ja rypälesiirapin kanssa; pinnalle rusinoita, pinjansiemeniä ja sipulia.
instructions: Suolaa ja paahda porsas.
Survo kastikkeen aineet ja kuumenna. Kaada paistin päälle.
Ripottele pinnalle rusinat, pinjansiemenet ja sipuli.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Roast the pig carefully; make thus a mortar mixture: pound pepper, dill, origany, green coriander, moisten with honey, wine, broth, oil, vinegar, reduced must. All of this when hot pour over [the roast] sprinkle raisins, pine nuts and chopped onions over and so serve.

recipes.title: Porsas viinikastikkeessa laakerilla
recipes.description: Marinoitu porsas paahdetaan öljyssä ja garumissa; kastike pippurista, ruudasta, laakerinmarjoista, garumista, makeasta viinistä ja vanhasta viinistä.
instructions: Marinoi ja paahda porsas öljyssä ja kalakastikkeessa.
Survo mausteet ja sekoita viineihin. Kuumenna.
Asettele porsas komealle vadille ja tarjoa kastikkeen kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Take the pig, garnish [with a marinade of herbs, etc.] cook [roast] it with oil and broth. When done, put in the mortar pepper, rue, laurel berries, broth, raisin wine or reduced wine, old wine, crush all, mix and prepare to a point; dress the pig on a showy service [2] platter and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] i.e. {oe}nococtum, cooked or prepared in wine sauce. [2] Dann. is of the opinion that the pig is cooked in a copper vessel, because the instructions are to serve it in patinam aheneam.

recipes.title: Porsas omassa paistoliemessään
recipes.description: Porsas paahdetaan omassa liemessään; liemi suurustetaan ja tarjotaan kastikekulhosta.
instructions: Paahda porsas uunissa vuoassa veden kanssa.
Nosta liha pois, suurusta paistoliemi, siivilöi ja tarjoa kastikekulhosta.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Roast the pig in its own juice; [when done] retire; bind the gravy with roux; [strain] put in a sauce boat and serve.

recipes.title: Timjamiporsas
recipes.originalTitle: Pig sprinkled with thyme (PORCELLUM THYMO SPARSUM)
recipes.description: Suolan ja tillin kanssa keitetty porsas jäähdytetään kylmässä vedessä vaaleana ja ripotellaan kynteliällä, timjamilla, kovaksi keitetyillä munilla ja sipulilla; kastike garumista, viinistä ja öljystä.
instructions: Keitä porsas suolavedessä tillin kanssa kypsäksi ja jäähdytä kylmässä vedessä, jotta pinta pysyy vaaleana.
Hienonna yrtit, munat ja sipuli ja ripottele valutetun porsaan päälle.
Valele kalakastikkeen, viinin ja öljyn seoksella.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Milk-fed pig, killed on the previous day, boil with salt and dill; transfer it into cold water, carefully keeping it submerged, to preserve its whiteness. Thereupon [make a cold dressing of the following] green savory herbs, [fresh] thyme, a little fleabane, hard boiled eggs, onions, [everything] chopped fine, sprinkle everything [over the pig which has been taken out of the water and allowed to drip off] and season with a pint of broth, one measure of oil, one of raisin wine, and so present it [1].

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] We would first mix the liquid components of this dressing with the chopped ingredients and then spread the finished dressing over the pig. Our author, no doubt, had this very process in mind.

recipes.title: Hapan porsas (porcellus oxyzomus)
recipes.description: Porsas haudutetaan liemessä, jossa 50 pippurinjyvää, hunajaa, kuivattua sipulia, korianteria, garumia, öljyä ja vettä; liemi sekoitellen sakeaksi.
instructions: Survo pippuri, hunaja, sipulit ja korianteri ja sekoita kalakastikkeeseen, öljyyn ja veteen.
Laita porsas pataan liemen kanssa ja hauduta. Sekoita lientä usein, jotta se sakenee.
Lisää lopuksi etikka ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Garnish [prepare and marinate] the pig correctly and place it in a liquor prepared as follows: put in the mortar 50 grains of pepper, as much honey [2] as is required, 3 dry onions, a little green or dry coriander, a pint of broth, 1 sextarius of oil, 1 pint of water; [all this] put in a stew pan [braisière] place the pig in it; when it commences to boil, stir the gravy quite frequently [3] so as to thicken it. Should the broth thus be reduced [by evaporation] add another pint of water. In this manner cook [braise] the pig to perfection and serve it.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] exodionum, and in the Summary of Dishes, exozome, i.e. oxyzomum. It is curious to note the various spellings and meanings of oxyzomum. This is supposed to be a sour sauce or an acid preparation of some kind, yet this recipe does not mention acids. In fact, the presence of honey would make it a sweet preparation. We take it, the "garnish" contains the necessary vinegar or other acids such as lemon juice, wine, etc. Oxyzomum is properly rendered "pickle." [2] Dann. oil, occurring twice in his version. [3] sæpius; Dann. confusing sæpe with cæpa, renders this "onions sauce." The same occurs to him in XXVII.

recipes.title: Porsas asafetidakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Paahdetun porsaan päälle kastike pippurista, lipstikasta, kuminasta, asafetidasta, pinjansiemenistä, taateleista, hunajasta, etikasta, garumista, sinapista ja öljystä.
instructions: Suolaa ja paahda porsas.
Survo kastikkeen aineet ja kaada paistin päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: In the mortar pound pepper, lovage, carraway, a little cumin, live laser, laser root, moisten with vinegar, add pine nuts, figdates, honey, vinegar, broth, prepared mustard, finish with oil to taste, and pour over [the roast pig].

recipes.title: Porsas aniksi-korianterikastikkeessa
recipes.description: Kastike pippurista, lipstikasta tai aniksesta, korianterista, ruudasta ja laakerista garumin, purjon, makean viinin, hunajan, viinin ja öljyn kanssa; suurustetaan.
instructions: Suolaa ja paahda porsas.
Survo mausteet, lisää purjo, kalakastike, viinit, hunaja, öljy ja vesi ja keitä. Suurusta.
Tarjoa kastike porsaan kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: In the mortar put pepper, lovage, or anise, coriander, rue, a laurel berry, pound [all], moistening with broth, [add] leeks, raisin wine, or a little honey, a little wine, and a like amount of oil. When this has been cooked tie with roux.

recipes.title: Yksinkertainen karitsa purjolla ja korianterilla
recipes.description: Karitsan pienet kyljykset haudutetaan öljyssä, garumissa ja viinissä purjon ja korianterin kanssa usein sekoittaen.
instructions: Laita kyljykset kattilaan öljyn, kalakastikkeen, viinin, purjon ja korianterin kanssa.
Kun liemi kiehuu, sekoita usein ja hauduta kypsäksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Of the skinned lamb make small cutlets which wash carefully and arrange in a sauce pan, add oil, broth, wine, leeks, coriander cut with the knife; when it commences to boil, stir very frequently [2] and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Unquestionably the ancient equivalent for "Irish Stew." [2] Cf. note 3 to {Rx} 492, XXIV; the presence of onion, however, would do no harm here.

recipes.title: Asafetidakili laakerilla
recipes.description: Kili tai karitsa täytetään pippuri-asafetida-öljyseoksella, paahdetaan kokonaisena ja tarjotaan ruudan ja laakerinmarjojen kanssa omassa paistoliemessään.
instructions: Leikkaa paistiin tasku ja täytä pippurin, kalakastikkeen, asafetidan ja öljyn seoksella. Sido.
Paahda 175 asteessa noin 1,5 tuntia.
Survo ruuta ja laakeri ja tarjoa lihan ja paistoliemen kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The well-cleaned guts of a kid fill with [a preparation of] pepper, broth, laser, oil [1], and put them back into the carcass which sew tightly and thus cook [roast] the kid [whole]. When done put in the mortar rue, laurel berries, and then serve the kid which meanwhile has been retired from the pot with its own drippings or gravy.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] There being only liquids for this filling of the guts, a more solid substance, such as pork forcemeat, eggs, or cereals would be required to make an acceptable filling for the casings of the kid. Furthermore sausage, for such is this in fact, must be thoroughly cooked before it can be used for the filling of the carcass, as not sufficient heat would penetrate the interior during the roasting to cook any raw dressing.

recipes.title: ”Terveysrastaat” tilli-purjoliemessä
recipes.description: Pikkulinnut täytetään pippurilla, asafetidalla, laakerilla, kuminalla ja garumilla, sidotaan ja keitetään öljyssä, suolassa, vedessä, tillissä ja purjossa (nykyään viiriäisillä).
instructions: Sekoita pippuri, asafetida, laakeri, kumina ja kalakastike ja täytä linnut. Sido.
Keitä linnut öljyn, suolan, veden, tillin ja purjon liemessä kypsiksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush pepper, laser, laurel berry, mix in cumin [2] garum and stuff the thrush [with this preparation, [3]] through the throat [4], tying them with a string. Thereupon make this preparation in which they are cooked: consisting of oil, salt, water [5], dill and heads of leeks.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] Cf. Summary of Dishes; term not identified, derived from the Greek, meaning to drive away all stomach ills. [2] We use juniper berries today instead of cumin. [3] Cf. note to {Rx} 496, XXVIII. [4] Thrush and other game birds of such small size are not emptied in the usual way: they are cooked with the entrails, or, the intestines are taken out, seasoned, sauté, and are either put back into the carcasses, or are served separately on bread croutons. In this instance, the necessary seasoning is introduced through the throat, a most ingenious idea that can only occur to Apicius. [5] In other instances we have pointed out where a small amount of water was used to clarify the oil used for frying foods. The presence here of water leads us to believe that the thrush were not "cooked," i.e. "boiled" but that they were fried in a generous amount of oil; this would make the ancient process remarkably similar to the present European way of preparing thrush or fieldfare, or similar game birds. For water used to clarify oil see note 3 to {Rx} No. 250.

recipes.title: Turturikyyhkyset asafetidamarinadissa
recipes.description: Linnut marinoidaan pippurin, asafetidan ja garumin seoksessa, jotta ne imevät maun, ja paahdetaan (nykyään viiriäisillä tai kyyhkysillä).
instructions: Halkaise ja puhdista linnut.
Marinoi pippurin, asafetidan, kalakastikkeen ja öljyn seoksessa muutama tunti.
Paahda 200 asteessa kypsiksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Open them, prepare [marinate] carefully; crush pepper, laser, a little broth, immerse the doves in this preparation so that it will be absorbed by them, and thus roast them.

recipes.title: Peltopyykastike sellerillä ja mintulla
recipes.description: Kirjan viimeinen ohje: pippuria, selleriä, minttua ja ruutaa etikassa, taateliviiniä, hunajaa, garumia ja öljyä keitettynä.
instructions: Survo mausteet ja yrtit etikan kanssa.
Lisää makea viini, hunaja, kalakastike ja öljy ja kiehauta.
Tarjoa lintujen kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Crush in the mortar pepper, celery, mint, and rue; moisten with vinegar, add figdate [wine], honey, vinegar, broth, oil; let it boil likewise and serve.

Selityksiä (Vehling 1936):

[1] This formula evidently is a fragment.
